bodyEn: Andoni Iraola said he will instruct Liverpool players to go down in the box in future after Alexander Isak was denied a penalty during Arsenal’s first win at Anfield for 14 years.

Liverpool were beaten by Kai Havertz’s early strike after a poor clearance from the goalkeeper ­Alisson but had two penalty claims dismissed by the referee, Andy Madley. The first, a shirt-pull by the Arsenal defender Jurriën Timber on Isak, prevented the ­Sweden international reaching Bradley Barcola’s cross. The second, a hold by Christos ­Tzolis on Cody Gakpo, was reviewed by the video assistant referee, Stuart Attwell, but rejected.

Isak stood his ground when held by Timber and Iraola claimed that counted against his team. Asked whether Isak should have collapsed in the area, the Liverpool head coach replied: “It’s a shame you ask me this question but, honestly, yes, we have to tell them to go down because they’re not going to call it otherwise.

“And then referees complain why they go down. Because if you don’t go down, you don’t call it. I think Alex is honest. He tries to go for the ball, everyone can see live straight away there is a clear, clear pull.”

Iraola accepted the reasons for ­dismissing the Gakpo penalty claim but believed they were inconsistent with the explanation for not ­awarding the Isak appeal. “I think there are two situations and they are a bit related,” he said.

“The Isak one is a clear penalty. He is going to head the ball in front of the goal and they grab him where ­everyone sees the shirt. The ball just goes in front of Alex and I don’t see the reason why [it isn’t given]. ­

“Probably because he doesn’t dive or he doesn’t go to the floor. It shouldn’t be a reason not to concede a penalty. The Gakpo one, I think it’s a sustained holding but I understand their argument and I think they are right when they say the ball was too long in the air and Cody wouldn’t have arrived to the ball.
“But then you’re basically ­accepting that the first one is a ­penalty, no? You cannot use the ­argument in both ways differently.”

Iraola’s post-match mood ­contrasted starkly with his childhood friend Mikel Arteta. The Arsenal ­manager, who claimed not to have seen the Isak incident, was elated by his team’s reaction to their Carabao Cup exit at Fleetwood in midweek and his first win at Anfield in charge of the Gunners.
Arteta said: “It feels better as a manager [to win at Anfield] because it has been such a long time without this feeling. I am extremely proud, especially given the conditions we arrived to the game.

“The defeat against Fleetwood looks like the end of the world but then you have to pick yourself up. That is the beautiful part of this game. Four days later you have to come to Anfield, and play against this manager, this team who are in a good moment, and so I am so proud of what my team has done.”
Arsenal have now won at four grounds where they did not win when securing the title last season – Anfield, Villa Park, the Stadium of Light and the City Ground.

“This is a mission we didn’t complete for 14 years,” Arteta said. “There were reasons for that. Some were ­psychological, some were related to the quality we showed on the pitch, and some were decisions. We knew we had to nail all of them. We knew we would have to navigate periods where we had to suffer.”

When informed that his team had denied Liverpool a shot on target in a Premier League game for the first time in 16 years, Arteta said: “I didn’t know about that stat but that is incredible. It didn’t feel like that at the time, they are a team that shoots a lot so you have to be good at denying them space and blocking shots. To do that against this team is remarkable, I would say.”

items.titleZh: 伊劳拉：我们必须告诉球员在禁区里倒地
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳时隔14年客胜利物浦，伊劳拉抱怨伊萨克未获点球并称以后会要求队员倒地。
bodyZh: 在阿森纳时隔14年首次在安菲尔德取胜的比赛中，亚历山大·伊萨克被拒绝了一次点球判罚，安多尼·伊劳拉表示，他未来将指示利物浦球员在禁区内倒地。
利物浦因门将阿利松解围失误被哈弗茨开场破门击败，但主裁判安迪·马德利拒绝了他们的两次点球诉求。第一次是阿森纳后卫尤里恩·廷贝尔拉扯伊萨克球衣，阻止了这位瑞典国脚接应布拉德利·巴尔科拉的传中。第二次是克里斯托斯·齐奥利斯对科迪·加克波的拉拽，经视频助理裁判斯图尔特·阿特维尔复核后被驳回。
伊萨克在被廷贝尔拉拽时站稳了脚跟，伊劳拉称这对其球队不利。当被问及伊萨克是否应该在禁区内倒地时，这位利物浦主帅回答说：“很遗憾你问我这个问题，但说实话，是的，我们必须告诉他们倒地，因为否则裁判不会判罚。”
“然后裁判又抱怨球员为什么倒地。因为如果你不倒地，他们就不吹。我认为亚历斯很诚实。他试图去争抢皮球，每个人都能在直播中立刻看到有一个非常明显的拉拽。”
伊劳拉接受了驳回加克波点球诉求的理由，但认为这与未判罚伊萨克犯规的解释不一致。“我认为有两种情况，它们有点相关，”他说。
“伊萨克那次是明显的点球。他准备在门前头球攻门，而对方拉扯了他的球衣，所有人都看到了。皮球正好落在亚历斯面前，我看不出为什么不判的原因。”
“可能是因为他没有假摔或者没有倒地。这不应成为不判点球的理由。至于加克波那次，我认为这是一次持续的拉拽，但我理解他们的论点，我也认为他们说皮球在空中飞行时间太长、科迪无法触及皮球的观点是正确的。”
“但那样的话，你基本上就承认了第一次是点球，对吧？你不能用两种不同的方式来使用这个论点。”
伊劳拉赛后的情绪与他的童年好友米克尔·阿尔特塔形成鲜明对比。这位阿森纳主教练声称没有看到伊萨克的事发经过，他对球队从周中联赛杯被弗利特伍德淘汰的阴影中恢复过来、以及执教枪手首胜安菲尔德感到欣喜若狂。
阿尔特塔说：“作为一名主教练（在安菲尔德赢球）感觉更好，因为已经有这么长时间没有这种感觉了。我感到极度自豪，特别是考虑到我们来到这里时的状况。”

“输给弗利特伍德看起来像是世界末日，但随后你必须振作起来。这就是这项运动美丽的部分。四天后你必须来到安菲尔德，与这位主教练、这支状态正佳的球队比赛，所以我为我的球队所做的一切感到非常骄傲。”
阿森纳现在已经在上赛季夺冠时未能取胜的四个球场赢球——安菲尔德、维拉公园球场、光明球场和城市球场。
“这是我们14年来未完成的任务，”阿尔特塔说。“这其中有原因。有些是心理上的，有些与我们在球场上展现出的质量有关，还有一些是判罚决定。我们知道我们必须把所有这些都做好。我们知道我们必须度过必须经受煎熬的时期。”
当得知他的球队16年来首次在英超比赛中零封利物浦的射正次数时，阿尔特塔说：“我之前不知道这个数据，但这太不可思议了。当时感觉并非如此，他们是一支射门很多的球队，所以你必须擅长限制他们的空间并封堵射门。对这支球队做到这一点是非常了不起的，我想这么说。”

bodyEn: Andoni Iraola had swatted aside any question that veered in the direction of Liverpool’s title credentials during his press conference on Friday with two simple words. “Too early,” he would respond. The Liverpool head coach was dismissive in terms of the stage of the season but, as Arsenal doggedly demonstrated, too early also applies to the development of his team.

Arsenal cavorted to the sound of fury at Anfield. At the final whistle Mikel Arteta leapt into the arms of the first-team coach Gabriel Heinze as he celebrated the release of his first win at Liverpool as Arsenal manager, his club’s first league victory at Anfield in 14 years and the champions moving three points clear at the top of the table. His players, tireless in the protection of Kai Havertz’s early winner, lined up to accept the acclaim from a jubilant away section. Anger filled the space around them.

From Virgil van Dijk collecting a post-match booking for sarcastically applauding the referee, Andy Madley, to the jeers of the home crowd, enraged by the match officials and most of all by Arsenal’s streetwise tactics/shithousery (delete as appropriate), this was an infuriating evening for a team that had arrived with momentum and amid talk of a potential title challenge. There was only applause for Liverpool’s players as they left the pitch in recognition of their effort and misfortune.

The hosts should have had a penalty for Jurriën Timber tugging Alexander Isak’s shirt and preventing him from connecting with a Bradley Barcola cross. Florian Wirtz struck the crossbar during Liverpool’s brightest spell and Alexis Mac Allister squandered a free header from 10 yards out. But as the second half ticked by and Arsenal absorbed the pressure, with Gabriel Magalhães and Declan Rice to the fore, belief in Liverpool’s powers of recovery faded.

There was no clearer sign of an expensively assembled team running out of ideas than Van Dijk operating as a makeshift centre‑forward in the final exchanges. He had Isak, Barcola and the substitutes Lewis Koumas, Victor Muñoz and Rio Ngumoha in support. Ngumoha had an impact but, ultimately, Liverpool’s varied forward line did not. For the first time in 16 years Liverpool failed to register a shot on target in a Premier League game.

Iraola’s complaint about Liverpool’s two defeats this season both turning on contentious refereeing decisions was valid. But he ended that particular discussion with a telling point. “I think it’s a penalty but we need to think about what we can improve to be on the right side of these big games,” Iraola admitted.

Another slow start cost Liverpool but they also lacked the penetration and the defensive might that underpinned Arsenal’s win. That will come in time under Iraola. In the meantime, there will be harsh lessons to occasionally absorb.

The Liverpool head coach again showed he is prepared to trust and reward young talent by handing a first start in the Premier League to Trey Nyoni. It was a bold call from Iraola, with Ryan Gravenberch dropped to the bench alongside the fit-again Dominik Szoboszlai to accommodate the 19-year-old, but one based on merit. Nyoni impressed Iraola from the moment he walked into the club this summer and stepped up a level on Liverpool’s pre-season tour of the US. The debut had been coming, and there was added weight to the vote of confidence that it should come against such formidable opposition.

Nyoni made his presence felt immediately. One reservation over the midfielder’s inclusion against a midfield of Rice, Bruno Guimarães and Martin Ødegaard was whether he had the physicality to compete. After merely 49 seconds he left Ødegaard in a heap to concede the game’s first free-kick. In the 10th minute he caught Havertz’s ankle with a late challenge and was perhaps fortunate to avoid the game’s first booking.

Nyoni’s timing was more accurate, his speed and strength clear, when beating Ødegaard convincingly in a 50‑50 challenge as they closed in on a David Raya throw. Arsenal rightly survived a video assistant referee’s check for a penalty against Christos Tzolis in the spell of pressure that followed Nyoni’s intervention.

The youngster’s composure on the ball and intelligent reading of the game were the most encouraging aspects of his full league debut. What worked against Nyoni, however, was Liverpool’s need to chase the game from as early as the 16th minute. Iraola needed attacking aggression and chaos in the final third more than the teenager’s defensive protection and patient buildup play. It was a reflection of the circumstances, not Nyoni’s own contribution, when he was replaced by Szoboszlai in the 59th minute.

There was chaos but no clarity to Liverpool’s performance in the final third, however. Despite the anguish over the antics of Gabriel, Havertz and the performance of Madley, there was a gap between the champions and potential contenders. Too early, as Iraola would say. But give it time.

items.titleZh: 经验丰富的卫冕冠军让利物浦的建队工作无功而返
items.summaryZh: 阿尔特塔带队在安菲尔德取胜，阿森纳在榜首领先三分。
bodyZh: 伊劳拉在周五的新闻发布会上用两个简单的词挡住了任何偏向利物浦争冠资格的问题。他回应道：“为时尚早。”这位利物浦主帅对赛季的阶段不屑一顾，但正如阿森纳顽强证明的那样，“为时尚早”也同样适用于他球队的发展。
阿森纳在安菲尔德的狂热欢呼中尽情庆祝。终场哨响时，米克尔·阿尔特塔跃入一线队教练加布里埃尔·海因策的怀抱，庆祝他作为阿森纳主帅在利物浦取得的首场胜利，这也是该俱乐部14年来首次在安菲尔德赢得联赛胜利，并且让卫冕冠军在积分榜榜首建立了三分的领先优势。他的球员们不知疲倦地守护着哈弗茨早早取得的进球，排队接受欢欣鼓舞的客场球迷的欢呼。愤怒充斥着他们周围的空间。
从范戴克因讽刺性地鼓掌主裁判安迪·马德利而吃到战后黄牌，到主场球迷的嘘声——他们对比赛官员感到愤怒，最重要的是对阿森纳老练的战术感到愤怒，对于一支带着势头并伴随着潜在争冠话题来到这里的球队来说，这是一个令人愤怒的夜晚。当利物浦球员离开球场时，只有掌声以表彰他们的努力和不幸。
由于廷贝尔拉扯伊萨克的球衣并阻止他接应巴尔科拉的传中，主队本应获得一个点球。维尔茨在利物浦表现最出色的时段击中了横梁，麦卡利斯特则浪费了一次在10码外的无人盯防头球。但随着下半场流逝，阿森纳在加布里埃尔·马加良斯和赖斯的带领下顶住了压力，人们对利物浦反弹能力的信念逐渐消退。
在比赛最后阶段，范戴克客串中锋，这是这支昂贵组建的球队黔驴技穷的最明显信号。他有伊萨克、巴尔科拉以及替补上场的卢库马斯、穆尼奥斯和恩古莫哈提供支持。恩古莫哈产生了一些影响，但最终利物浦多变的锋线却没有。16年来，利物浦首次在英超比赛中没有射门命中目标。
伊劳拉对利物浦本赛季的两场失利都因有争议的裁判判罚而改变的抱怨是成立的。但他用一个意味深长的观点结束了那场讨论。“我认为这是一个点球，但我们需要思考如何改进才能站在这些重大比赛的正义一方，”伊劳拉承认道。
又一个慢热让利物浦付出了代价，但他们也缺乏支撑阿森纳取胜的穿透力和防守实力。在伊劳拉的带领下，这些终究会到来。与此同时，偶尔需要吸取严厉的教训。
利物浦主帅再次通过给特雷·尼奥尼首次英超首发出场机会，表明他准备信任并奖励年轻人才。这是伊劳拉的一个大胆决定，赫拉芬贝赫以及伤愈复出的索博斯洛伊都被降为替补，以为这位19岁的球员腾出空间，但这完全是基于实力。尼奥尼从今年夏天走进俱乐部的那一刻起就给伊劳拉留下了深刻印象，并在利物浦的美国季前赛中提升了一个水平。这场首秀本该到来，而面对如此强大的对手上演首秀，更增加了这份信任票的分量。
尼奥尼立即宣示了自己的存在。对于这位中场球员在面对赖斯、布鲁诺·吉马良斯和厄德合组成的中场时是否具备竞争的身体对抗能力，人们曾心存疑虑。仅仅49秒后，他就将厄德高撞倒在地，送出了本场比赛的第一个任意球。在第10分钟，他的一次迟到铲断踢到了哈弗茨的脚踝，或许很幸运地避免了本场比赛的第一张黄牌。

当尼奥尼在争抢大卫· Raya的界外球时，在50对50的拼抢中令人信服地击败了厄德高，他的时机更加准确，速度和力量也十分清晰。在尼奥尼干预后的高压时段，阿森纳通过了视频助理裁判对针对齐奥利犯规的越位/点球检查，这是应得的。
这位年轻人在控球时的冷静和对比赛的聪明阅读是他完整的英超首秀中最令人鼓舞的方面。然而，对尼奥尼不利的是利物浦从第16分钟就开始追赶比分的需要。比起这位少年的防守保护和耐心组织，伊劳拉更需要前场的进攻侵略性和混乱。当他在第59分钟被索博斯洛伊换下时，这反映了当时的形势，而不是尼奥尼自己的贡献。
然而，利物浦在前场的表现一片混乱，毫无清晰度。尽管对加布里埃尔、哈弗茨的花招以及马德利的表现感到痛苦，但卫冕冠军与潜在争夺者之间还是存在差距。正如伊劳拉所说，为时尚早。但给它点时间。

items.titleEn: Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal: Premier League – as it happened
items.summaryEn: Kai Havertz’s goal was enough to give Arsenal their first win at Anfield since September 2012 and take them three points clear at the top of the tableSo where is the game? Liverpool will look to get men around the ball when Arsenal have it, opening the pitch for switches should they win possession. And when they don’t, they’ll run like mad to recover it, stretching play and passing forwards, facilitating that by conserving energy every now and again when Nyoni slows the game down.In particular, I expect they’ll ask Bradley Barcola to target the space left when Riccardo Calafiori goes off on adventures, with Alexander Isak pulling away for cut-backs and shooting quickly with little backlift, while Florian Wirtz looks to slip passes in behind – if he can work quickly enough in the maelstrom of the match. Continue reading...
bodyEn: Aha, David Hytner’s match report is with us.
That means we’re finished here, so thanks for all your company and comments – sorry I couldn’t use them all – and peace out.

Van Dijk tells Sky Liverpool could’ve done more in the last 15 minutes but is disappointed. He thinks they played better after conceding, Mac Allister’s header could’ve changed the game, and he thinks it was a clear penalty on Isak.
Asked if Isak should’ve complained more, he says there are plenty of cameras, so well done to Arsenal.

When someone new comes in, he says, it needs time, work, going through difficult moments and so on. The fans can see there’s so much improvement already in recent weeks, they work their socks off, which is the bare minimum, especially at Liverpool, and what they need is results.

“Not forceful or violent” was VAR’s verdict on Madueke’s little nodlet on Mac Allister. I think that’s the correct call, but again, we need to do something with the laws; currently, we seem to have instituted a system whereby minor off-ball offences and general petulance are judged more harshly than tackles which can cause injury.
I guess Wirtz was signed to be that, but it doesn’t look like he can work quickly enough to compensate for his lack of power and explosive speed.
On the other hand, there are young players coming through who might change that – Max Dowman and Rio Ngumoha most particularly.

That game was, by the way, exactly why I said the Premier League lacks attacking quality. Watching two of the most expensively assembled teams in history, we saw very little in terms of wit, interplay and individual improvisation. The speed, intensity and physicality were something, but neither side had a player able to make sense of it all.
Also going on:
Declan Rice says Anfield creates waves of sustained attacks, but they got off to a good start and their togetherness is “undefeated … like nothing I’ve ever seen before”.

Haveertz says Liverpool have top players and can show their quality, but they stuck together, defended together, and there were tough moments. On the goal, he says 90% of it belongs to Rice – “we all know his right foot”.

Back to Rice, he says the manager “had a really honest conversation” with him at the start of the season, telling him he could do more, and before the game, he told Havertz to attack the box. It’s his first win at Anfield, but it doesn’t mean anything in terms of the table; you take it seriously in February and March. Before that, you just win as many games as you can.
Rice is given player of the match and, though I’d have gone for Gabriel, I can’t argue with that.

“They just fell short,” says Adam Darke, but the truth is Liverpool weren’t really close. Opta have just decided that Barcola shot does’t count as one, so they went 96 minutes at home without mustering one; they had the Mac Allister header over the bar and Wirtz’s free-kick that hit the bar, but pretty much nothing else.
Or, put another way, Iraola has work to do – but they won’t play teams who defend like Arsenal every week.

Arsenal win at Anfield for the first time since September 2012; Mikel Arteta wins at Arsenal for the first time in his managerial career. They move top of the table thanks to a colossal effort of collective organisation and defending; it’ll take something significant to stop them retaining their title.
90+6 min Szoboszlai moves it forward, Tsimikas’ attempted cross is blocked by Madueke, and when the ball is pumped back into the Arsenal box, Raya quickly gathers.
90+5 min Alisson punts downfield, Van Dijk makes first contact, and Isak is penalised for a foul on Gabriel. That will probably be it.
90+4 min Two more minutes and, if they don’t concede, Arsenal are going clear at the top. This has been a monstrous rearguard, even if they’ve not been confronted with much quality.
90+2 min Barcola trickles a shot that Raya fields easily; that’s their first one on target. Raya is booked shortly afterwards for wasting time.

90+1 min The corner is cleared so Liverpool come again, but they ran out of ideas some time ago;, if indeed they ever really had any beyond sticking balls into the box. They’v been decent up until that point, but I’m not sure why they’re constructing attacks exactly as Arsenal want them to.

90 min Another ball tossed into the box, Van Dijk flicks on, ands Munoz inhales to squeeze between Calafiori and Hincapie, but can’t get enough on his header. But Liverpool sustain the attack, Ngumoha’s cross blocked behind for a corner; we’ll have six additional minutes.

89 min Arteta sends on Merino for Odegaard, and this reminds me a little of the Bayern game last season, Arsenal securing victory by sending on athletes. They lack a little bit finesse, as Wenger might’ve said but playing them is no fun for anyone.
88 min I thoght Gyokeres might’ve come on earlier to run channels, and when Szoboszlai runs into Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly has a chance to hit him … but puts too much on the pass.

86 min This has been a disappointing second half from Liverpool. The link-up play around the box hasn’t been good enough, but also, they haven’t attempted enough of it. But here’s Ngumoha, running at Calafiori and tossing a few lollipops, his shot blocked out for a throw; Van Dijk is now playing centre-forward, so expect yet more crosses.
84 min Changes for Arsenal, Hincapie and Gyokeres for Tzolis and Havertz. Havertz isn’t everyone’s idea of a centre-forward, mine included, but his record in big games is superb.
82 min Ch ch changes for Liverpool, Munoz, who’ll play right-back, Koumas and Tsimikas on, with Araujo, Wirtz and Kerkez off.
81 min VAR makes the call to let things be; good. Mac Allister and Timber are both booked; the former should be ashamed of the show he made of himself.

79 min Mac Allister fouls Odegaard, then bends double to get in his face, applying a minor slap for extra aggravation. Naturally, sentiments are then exchanges, Timber to the fore, then Madueke puts a forehead next to Mac Aillster’s; I’m not sure there’s forward motion, but there is minor contact, Mac Allister goes down like he’s been deflated, and VAR has a decision to make.

77 min But in the meantime, Ngumoha comes in on his weaker foot, crossing to the back post, and when the ball is knocked back by Van Dijk, Araujo tries to muscle a shot but it bloicked off at source. Liverpool still haven’t had a shot on target which tells you plenty about Arsenal’s defending – and their lack of slickness when it really counts.

75 min Ngumoha conjures space down the right but can’t quite find a gap big enough to sneak through. I wonder if, at some point soon, Iraola might swap him with Barcola, who has the speed to get down the outside, so he can attack the diagonal angle towards the box.
74 min I meant to say, Lewis-Skelly was booked a few minutes ago for bouncing Isak.

73 min Arsenal are starting to control things and, as I type, Madueke moves down the left, sliding square to Tzolis on the other side. He opens the angle for a curler, pinging it low and had … forcing Alisson to plunge right to tip around the post.

71 min Kerkez has to go off after taking treatment; he’s off for quite some time and, in the meantime, Calafiori goes down the left, crosses low, and Van Dijk does really well to insert himself in front of Tzolis, poking away from his slide.

68 mins Jacquet slips and Tzolis is in behind down the left! Alisson leaves space at his near post too, and sure’y he’s going to shoot, but instead he squares, seeking Odegaard, only for the recovering Jacquet to slide in and intercept. He has settled brilliantly; as with many things, I think Richie Aprile said it best.

68 min For a team that doesn’t exude joy, I take pleasure i how much sick pleasure Arsenal take in defending. They love the conflict and confrontation, expect themselves to repel attacks, and do anything to back each other up.
67 min It’s time: Ngumoha replaces Gakpo.
66 min Barcola teleports down the left, crosses low, and Wirtz’s touch is poor then, when Madueke carries clear, Kerkez trips him and is booked.

63 min It’s a while since Liverpool created a proper a chance, and the crowd try to get them going. Arsenal have made the game all Bitty McLean these last few minutes, and they can feel the sweat of time expiring.
62 min Change for Arsenal, Lewis-Skelly on for Guimaraes. I think Arteta will want his ability to get the ball up the pitch.

60 min “I don’t buy this line that all of the best attacking players play outside of the Premier League, writes David Wall.” Sure, Lamine Yamal, Kvaratskhelia, and Mbappe are perhaps on another level (I’d argue Dembele is more of a team player than a great individualist). But others are no better than the best in the Premier League, they just look more glamorous in the colours of Real Madrid or Barcelona. For instance, Anthony Gordon has looked brilliant for Barca so far but was average and inconsistent for Newcastle last year. Players like Haarland, Isak, Bruno Fernande (albeit not this year), Saka, Odegaard, and a few others are as individually talented or effective as anyone playing outside the Premier League. They just suffer through familiarity.”

But that’s what I said: the best attackers don’t play in the Prem. You gave a list, and to that we can add Kane, Olise, Bellingham, Raphinha and others. Saka and Odegaard aren’t in that class, while of course Gordon looks better playing in front of Pedri.

58 min Here comes the change, Szoboszlai returning from injury to replace Nyoni. He struggled to control his emotions early on and might’ve been sent off for two bookable offences, but he stabilised thereafter and kept things ticking with hard, simple passes.
57 min I wonder if we might see Ngumoha soon; oh, but on the touchline, Szoboszlai is preparing himself. Presumably, Nyoni will be the man to make way.
56 min Then Nyoni gives Kerkez quick, simple ball, and hew sets off diagonally from the touchline before slipping Isak in behind; from an acute angle, he thrashes over.
55 min Madueke sweeps Barcol’s legs and is booked.

53 min “Winning the league requires winning every week against teams who are almost uniformly top 40, probably top 30 in Europe,” writes Sam Glover. “It’s not glamorous but it’s just as hard as winning four must-wins against good rivals. It’s just a different era.

And how many top players come to the Premier League and crush it, against how many leave the league and crush it elsewhere. The top of the Champions League is just a reflection of the fact that English teams are battered week in, week out and their rivals play their second team in the league.”

I agree with all of this, but I still think the point stands: the standard at the top is not high. Arsenal aren’t close to Guardiola’s City, Klopp’s Liverpool, Mourinho’s Chelsea or Fergie’s two Champions League winners.

51 min We’ve carried on where we left off, Liverpool again peppering the Arsenal box with crosses, again to little avail. Oh but this is better, Nyoni punching into Mac Allister, who turns to Isak, who flicks around the corner for Kerkez … who’s offside. Nevertheless, those are the kind of moves Liverpool need to construct, one-touch passing against which Arsenal’s defence can’t set.
49 min Thinking again about Jasper’s email, the point with Isak isn’t so much about him taking a dive, but making enough of a confident fuss to make sure VAR take a serious look.
48 min Araujo, of whom we’ve seen relatively little, crosses, but the various attackers are on their heels.
items.author: Daniel Harris
items.titleZh: 利物浦 0-1 阿森纳：英超联赛实时战报
items.summaryZh: 哈弗茨进球助阿森纳客场击败利物浦，自2012年以来首次在安菲尔德取胜并登顶积分榜。
bodyZh: 啊哈，大卫·海特纳的比赛报告来了。
这意味着我们的直播到此结束，感谢大家的陪伴和评论——很抱歉没能用到所有的留言——大家再见。
范戴克对天空体育表示，利物浦在最后15分钟本可以做得更多，但他感到失望。他认为他们在失球后踢得更好，麦卡利斯特的头球本可以改变比赛，而且他认为那是一个对伊萨克的明显点球。
当被问及伊萨克是否应该更多地抱怨时，他说有很多摄像机，所以阿森纳做得很好。
他说，当新面孔加入时，需要时间、工作、经历困难时刻等等。球迷们可以看到最近几周已经有了很大的进步，他们拼尽全力，这是最起码的要求，尤其是在利物浦，他们需要的是结果。
VAR对马杜埃凯轻触麦卡利斯特的裁决是“不具攻击性或暴力”。我认为这是一个正确的判罚，但再次说明，我们需要对规则做点什么；目前，我们似乎建立了一种制度，即对无球状态下的轻微犯规和一般急躁情绪的判罚，比可能导致受伤的铲球还要严厉。
我猜Wirtz被签下是为了扮演这个角色，但他看起来无法以足够快的速度来弥补他力量和爆发力的不足。
另一方面，有一些年轻球员正在崭露头角，可能会改变这种状况——马克斯·多曼和里奥·恩古莫哈最为引人注目。
顺便说一句，那场比赛正是为什么我说英超缺乏进攻质量的原因。看着历史上两支身价最高球队的较量，我们在智慧、配合和个人即兴发挥方面几乎看不到什么。速度、强度和身体对抗确实很强，但双方都没有一个能把这一切串联起来的球员。
同时进行的还有：
德克兰·赖斯表示，安菲尔德会制造出一波又一波持续的进攻，但他们开局良好，他们的团结是“无敌的……就像我以前从未见过的那样”。
哈弗茨说利物浦拥有顶级球员并能展现他们的实力，但他们团结一致，共同防守，经历了一些艰难时刻。关于进球，他说90%归功于赖斯——“我们都知道他的右脚”。
回到赖斯，他说主教练在赛季初与他进行了“一次非常坦诚的对话”，告诉他可以做得更多，而在赛前，他告诉哈弗茨要冲击禁区。这是他在安菲尔德的首场胜利，但这并不意味着积分榜上的最终结果；你需要在2月和3月认真对待。在此之前，你只需尽可能赢得更多的比赛。
赖斯被评为全场最佳球员，尽管我会把这个荣誉给加布里埃尔，但我对此没有异议。
亚当·达克说：“他们只是功亏一篑，”但事实是利物浦并没有真正接近。Opta刚刚裁定巴尔科拉的射门不被算作一次射门，所以他们在主场有96分钟的时间没有完成一脚射门；他们有麦卡利斯特击中横梁上方的头球和维尔茨击中横梁的任意球，但几乎没有其他威胁。
或者换句话说，伊劳拉还有工作要做——但他们不会每周都遇到像阿森纳这样防守的球队。
阿森纳自2012年9月以来首次在安菲尔德取胜；米克尔·阿尔特塔在其执教生涯中首次在阿森纳客胜利物浦。凭借集体组织和防守的巨大努力，他们升至积分榜首；要阻止他们卫冕冠军，需要付出巨大的努力。
第90+6分钟，索博斯洛伊向前推进，齐米卡斯的传中尝试被马杜埃凯封堵，当球被重新吊入阿森纳禁区时，拉亚迅速将球没收。
第90+5分钟，阿利松大脚开到前场，范戴克争到第一落点，伊萨克因对加布里埃尔犯规被判犯规。比赛大概就这样了。
第90+4分钟，还剩两分钟，如果不再丢球，阿森纳将稳居榜首。这是一次极其顽强的后防表现，尽管他们并没有面对太多有质量的进攻。
第90+2分钟，巴尔科拉轻射被拉亚轻松化解；这是他们的第一脚射正。拉亚随后因拖延时间被黄牌警告。
第90+1分钟，角球被解围，利物浦卷土重来，但他们的办法在一段时间前就已经用尽了；如果他们除了把球吊入禁区之外真的有什么战术的话。在此之前他们的表现还算体面，但我不太明白他们为什么偏要按照阿森纳希望的方式组织进攻。
第90分钟，又一个球被吊入禁区，范戴克头球摆渡，穆尼奥斯试图在卡拉菲奥里和因卡皮耶之间钻过去抢点，但头球力量不足。不过利物浦延续了进攻，恩古莫哈的传中被封堵出底线获得角球；我们将有六分钟的补时。
第89分钟，阿尔特塔换上梅里诺换下厄德高，这让我想起了上赛季对阵拜仁的比赛，阿森纳通过换上身体强壮的球员来确保胜利。正如温格所说，他们可能缺乏一点细腻，但和他们比赛对任何人来说都不是件趣事。
第88分钟，我以为约克雷斯会早点上场去冲击防线，当索博斯洛伊撞倒厄德高时，刘易斯-斯凯利有机会对付他……但传球力量过大。
第86分钟，利物浦下半场的表现令人失望。禁区周边的配合不够好，而且他们尝试的次数也不够多。但恩古莫哈来了，他带球冲向卡拉菲奥里并晃动了几下，射门被封堵出边线；范戴克现在在踢中锋，所以预计会有更多的传中。
第84分钟，阿森纳做出换人调整，因卡皮耶和约克雷斯换下特佐利斯和哈弗茨。哈弗茨并不是每个人心目中的中锋人选，包括我在内，但他在重大比赛中的纪录是极好的。
第82分钟，利物浦进行人员调整，将踢右后卫的穆尼奥斯、库马斯和齐米卡斯换上，阿劳霍、维尔茨和克尔凯兹下场。
第81分钟，VAR维持原判；很好。麦卡利斯特和廷贝尔双双吃到黄牌；前者为自己的假摔表现感到羞耻。
第79分钟，麦卡利斯特对厄德高犯规，然后弯下腰贴到他脸上，并进行轻微的掌掴以激化矛盾。随后双方自然发生了口角，廷贝尔冲在前面，接着马杜埃凯将额头贴向麦卡利斯特；我不确定是否有前冲动作，但确实有轻微接触，麦卡利斯特像泄了气一样倒地，VAR需要做出裁决。
第77分钟，但与此同时，恩古莫哈用他的弱势脚内切，传中到后点，当范戴克将球顶回时，阿劳霍试图强行射门，但被直接封堵。利物浦仍然没有一脚射正，这充分说明了阿森纳的防守——以及他们在关键时刻缺乏流畅度。
第75分钟，恩古莫哈在右路创造出了空间，但找不到足够大的空当钻过去。我想不久后伊劳拉可能会让他与巴尔科拉对换位置，后者拥有从外线突破的速度，这样他就可以斜向冲击禁区。
第74分钟，我的意思是，刘易斯-斯凯利几分钟前因为撞倒伊萨克被黄牌警告。
第73分钟，阿森纳开始掌控局势，就在我打字的时候，马杜埃凯沿左路推进，横敲给另一侧的特佐利斯。他拉开角度起脚兜射，打出一记低平球……迫使阿利松倒地扑救将球挡出立柱。
第71分钟，克尔凯兹接受治疗后必须离场；他在场外呆了很长时间，与此同时，卡拉菲奥里从左路下底传出低平球，范戴克表现非常出色，抢在特佐利斯之前将球从他的滑铲中捅开。
第68分钟，雅凯滑倒，特佐利斯从左路获得单刀！阿利松在前门柱也留出了空间，他本该射门，但他却选择了横敲寻找厄德高，结果回追的雅凯滑铲将球拦截。他的表现极为出色；正如里奇·阿普里尔（Richie Aprile）所说的那样精辟。
第68分钟，对于一支不怎么流露喜悦的球队来说，我为阿森纳从防守中获得病态的快感而感到高兴。他们热爱冲突和对抗，期望自己能击退进攻，并不惜一切代价互相补位。
第67分钟，是时候了：恩古莫哈换下加克波。
第66分钟，巴尔科拉在左路如闪电般突破并送出低平球传中，维尔茨停球糟糕，随后当马杜埃凯带球突破时，克尔凯兹将其绊倒并吃到黄牌。
第63分钟，利物浦已经有一段时间没有创造出真正的机会了，现场球迷试图为主队加油助威。在过去的几分钟里，阿森纳把比赛变得支离破碎，利物浦能感受到时间流逝带来的煎熬。
第62分钟，阿森纳换人，刘易斯-斯凯利换下吉马良斯。我想阿尔特塔是需要他把球运过半场的能力。

第60分钟，“我不买账那种‘所有最佳进攻球员都在英超之外踢球’的说法，”大卫·沃尔写道。“当然，亚马尔、克瓦拉茨赫利亚和姆巴佩或许处于另一个水平（我认为登贝莱更像是一个团队球员，而不是伟大的个人主义者）。但其他球员并不比英超的顶尖球员差，他们只是身披皇马或巴萨球衣显得更有光彩。例如，安东尼·戈登在巴萨表现出色，但去年在纽卡斯尔却表现平平且不够稳定。像哈兰德、伊萨克、布鲁诺·费尔南德斯（尽管今年不是）、萨卡、厄德高以及其他一些球员，其个人才华或效率并不逊色于任何在英超之外踢球的人。他们只是受到了熟悉程度的影响。”
但这就是我所说的：最好的攻击手不在英超踢球。你列出了一份名单，对此我们还可以加上凯恩、奥利塞、贝林厄姆、拉菲尼亚等人。萨卡和厄德高不在那个级别，当然戈登在佩德里身边踢球看起来更好。
第58分钟，换人调整来了，索博斯洛伊伤愈复出替换恩约尼。他在比赛刚开始时情绪有些失控，本来可能因两次黄牌犯规被罚下，但此后他稳住了阵脚，通过简单硬朗的传球保持了节奏。
第57分钟，我想我们很快就能看到恩古莫哈登场了；哦，但在场边，索博斯洛伊正在做准备。据推测，恩约尼将是离场的人。
第56分钟，随后恩约尼给克尔凯兹送出一脚快速简单的传球，他从边线开始斜向带球突破，然后将球塞到伊萨克身后；从极小的角度，他将球抽高。
第55分钟，马杜埃凯绊倒巴尔科拉被黄牌警告。
第53分钟，“赢得联赛冠军需要在每个星期都战胜那些几乎全是欧洲前40、甚至可能是前30的球队，”萨姆·格洛弗写道。“这并不迷人，但它和在四场必须取胜的比赛中击败强敌一样艰难。这只是不同的时代。”
有多少顶级球员来到英超并大杀四方，又有多少人离开英超并在其他地方大杀四方。欧冠的巅峰只是英格兰球队每周饱受摧残、而他们的竞争对手在联赛中派上替补阵容的写照。
我同意所有这些观点，但我仍然认为重点没有变：顶尖水平并不算高。阿森纳远不及瓜迪奥拉的曼城、克洛普的利物浦、穆里尼奥的切尔西或弗格森的两支欧冠冠军球队。
第51分钟，我们回到了之前的节奏，利物浦再次用传中轰炸阿森纳禁区，但收效甚微。哦，不过这次好多了，恩约尼将球传给麦卡利斯特，后者转身传给伊萨克，伊萨克脚后跟磕给克尔凯兹……但他越位了。尽管如此，这正是利物浦需要建立的进攻套路，通过一脚传球来破解阿森纳无法落位的防守。
第49分钟，再次想到贾斯帕的邮件，关于伊萨克的关键不在于他是否假摔，而在于他要大惊小怪到足以让VAR认真审查的程度。
第48分钟，我们见之不多的阿劳霍送出传中，但多名攻击手反应不及。

bodyEn: It was a game when Arsenal showed their ruthless side and all of the champion knowhow that they accumulated over the course of last season. They headed back to London having made a statement. Irrespective of what happens to Manchester City over their financial rule breaches, Arsenal remain the Premier League’s team to beat.

Mikel Arteta was in the Arsenal midfield when the club last won a league fixture at Anfield; it was in September 2012, although his memories are a little hazy given the concussion that he sustained in a collision with Jordan Henderson.

Arteta has a clear-eyed focus on retaining the title and this was an occasion for his hopes to surge. Kai Havertz’s first goal in 10 appearances proved the difference but the victory was rooted in Arsenal’s capacity to control and frustrate.

It was a tough watch for the Liverpool crowd and they bayed throughout at what they perceived as Arsenal’s use of the dark arts. Arteta’s team won 18 free-kicks and there were some soft ones – each was the prompt for an eruption from the Kop. It said plenty that Virgil van Dijk responded to the full-time whistle by sarcastically applauding the referee, Andy Madley. The Liverpool captain was booked.

The home team had their grievances. Alexander Isak felt Jurriën Timber grab a handful of his shirt in the 21st minute as he tried to reach a Bradley Barcola cross in front of goal. It was a mystery as to why the video assistant referee did not alert Madley. Van Dijk could also be heard shouting in the tunnel afterwards at Noni Madueke, saying the Arsenal winger should have had a second yellow card.

Madueke, who was booked for a foul on Barcola, took a risk when he initiated a touch of foreheads with Alexis Mac Allister towards the end after a melee had broken out. It was sparked by Mac Allister’s furious reaction to Martin Ødegaard’s winning of a free-kick. Liverpool, however, lost any claim to the moral high ground when Mac Allister crumpled to the turf in an attempt to get Madueke sent off. The Arsenal player survived. It would have been a harsh dismissal.

In the final analysis, Liverpool did not do enough. They provided high‑energy enjoyment in the first half but they fizzled out, the invention drying up. They finished with no shots on target as their five-match winning run in all competitions ground to a halt. Goals remain a problem for them in the league and the truth was Arsenal kept them out with a measure of comfort. Arsenal’s previous trip to the north‑west had ended in Carabao Cup humiliation at Fleetwood on Tuesday night. This was much more like it.

Liverpool brought the intensity at the outset with Trey Nyoni snapping into challenges on his full league debut. The 19-year-old’s first action was to leave something on Ødegaard and, not long after that, he did the same to Havertz. Nyoni was fortunate to emerge without a yellow card.

The tone was set early, the Kop teeming with indignation at what they saw as Arsenal’s readiness to go down easily and stay down. The match was shaped by Havertz’s goal on 16 minutes and from a Liverpool point of view, it was a self-inflicted wound. Alisson tried to be too cute with a short pass out from his area for Jérémy Jacquet; the weight and direction of it was wrong. But when Ødegaard pounced, a stunning piece of interplay followed. Arsenal worked it over and up the right for Declan Rice to flash over the final ball, low and across the corridor of a six-yard box of uncertainty. Havertz, a player who needed an easy tap-in, got one.

Liverpool responded with more fire and they could have scored before the interval, Mac Allister blowing the big chance – a free header from Milos Kerkez’s cross in the 43rd minute. Moments earlier, Florian Wirtz had whipped a free-kick from the left‑hand side against the crossbar.

Arsenal flickered on the break. There were a few times in the first half when they flooded men forward and there were possibilities. This was a long way from being a smash‑and‑grab. Havertz narrowly failed to get a touch to a Bruno Guimarães cross-cum-shot while Timber could not react in front of goal after Madueke volleyed a Christos Tzolis cross back from an acute angle.

Arsenal had the match where they wanted it. They backed themselves to keep Liverpool at bay. It was about their game management. They have become masters at drawing the sting and the longer the second half went on the more assured Arsenal looked. They stifled Liverpool and there remained the sense they could land something on the counter.

When Jacquet slipped in the 68th minute, Arsenal went left to Tzolis and he almost teed up Ødegaard. With Alisson out of position, Jacquet got back to make an important intervention. Tzolis also forced an excellent save with a first‑time shot for the far corner. Liverpool fought a losing battle to keep a lid on their emotions. They huffed and they puffed. The equaliser never looked like coming.

items.titleZh: 阿森纳击败利物浦，终结2012年以来客场不胜纪录
items.summaryZh: 哈弗茨开场闪击破门，阿森纳客场战胜利物浦，取得2012年以来联赛客场首胜。
bodyZh: 这是一场阿森纳展现其冷酷一面以及上赛季积累的冠军经验的比赛。他们带着一份宣言返回伦敦。无论曼城因财务违规面临什么结果，阿森纳依然是英超最难被击败的球队。
阿尔特塔在2012年9月俱乐部上一次在安菲尔德赢得联赛胜利时还在阿森纳的中场踢球，尽管由于他与亨德森相撞导致轻微脑震荡，他的记忆有些模糊。
阿尔特塔对卫冕有着清晰的专注，这也是他满怀希望的时刻。哈弗茨在10场比赛中的首粒进球成为了分水岭，但胜利源于阿森纳控制和压制对手的能力。
对利物浦球迷而言这是一场艰难的比赛，他们整场比赛都在抗议阿森纳所谓的“黑暗艺术”。阿尔特塔的球队赢得了18次任意球，其中有一些比较软弱——每一次都引发了科普看台的爆发。范戴克在终场哨响时对裁判安迪·马德利进行讽刺性鼓掌说明了很多问题。利物浦队长吃到了黄牌。
主队有他们的怨言。亚历山大·伊萨克在第21分钟试图接应巴尔科拉的传中时，感觉廷贝尔在门前拉扯了他的球衣。视频助理裁判为何没有提醒马德利令人费解。随后还能听到范戴克在通道里对马杜埃凯大喊，称这位阿森纳边锋应该吃到第二张黄牌。
因对巴尔科拉犯规而染黄的马杜埃凯在一次冲突爆发后，于尾声阶段与麦卡利斯特发生头部接触，冒了很大风险。这次冲突由麦卡利斯特对厄德高赢得任意球的愤怒反应引发。然而，当麦卡利斯特为了罚下马杜埃凯而痛苦倒地时，利物浦失去了道德高地。这位阿森纳球员留在了场上。这本可能是一次严厉的罚下。
最终分析下来，利物浦做得还不够。他们在上半场展现了充满高能量的乐趣，但随后烟消云散，创造力枯竭。他们全场没有一次射正，各项赛事的五连胜就此终结。进球依然是他们联赛中的问题，事实是阿森纳相当从容地零封了他们。阿森纳上一次造访西北部是在周二晚上联赛杯客场不敌弗利特伍德遭遇羞辱。这次的表现要好得多。
利物浦在开场阶段就拿出了强度，年仅19岁的特雷·尼奥尼在其首次英超先发中凶狠拼抢。这位19岁球员的第一个动作就是放倒了厄德高，不久之后他又对哈弗茨如法炮制。尼奥尼很幸运没有吃到黄牌。
比赛基调很早就定下了，科普看台对阿森纳轻易倒地并赖在地上的做法充满愤怒。比赛由哈弗茨在第16分钟的进球塑造，从利物浦的角度来看，这是一记自摆乌龙。阿利森试图在禁区内给雅凯传出一脚过于精巧的短传；传球力量和方向都不对。但当厄德高机敏抢断后，随之而来的是一段惊艳的配合。阿森纳将球运作到右路，德克兰·赖斯送出低平横传掠过门前险区。哈弗茨需要一脚轻松的推射破门，他就得到了一个。

利物浦用更强烈的斗志作出回应，他们本可以在中场休息前得分，麦卡利斯特在第43分钟错失良机——接米洛斯·凯尔克兹传中头球顶高。片刻之前，维尔茨主罚左侧任意球击中横梁。
阿森纳在反击中闪光。上半场有好几次他们大举压上并创造了机会。这远非一场偷鸡摸狗的胜利。哈弗茨险些触及吉马良斯的传射，而廷贝尔在马杜埃凯从小角度将克里斯托斯·齐奥利斯的传中凌空垫回门前后也未能及时反应。
阿森纳将比赛掌控在他们想要的位置。他们坚信自己能够挡住利物浦。这关乎他们的比赛管理。他们已经成为消磨比赛大师，下半场时间越久，阿森纳看起来就越自信。他们压制了利物浦，并且始终让人觉得他们能在反击中给予致命一击。
当雅凯在第68分钟滑倒时，阿森纳将球打到左路寻找齐奥利斯，后者险些助攻厄德高。在阿利森失位的情况下，雅凯回追作出了关键解围。齐奥利斯还通过一脚远角劲射迫使门将做出精彩扑救。利物浦为控制情绪进行着一场注定失利的战斗。他们气喘吁吁。扳平比分的进球从未出现。

bodyEn: English football loves the word “dossier”. It doesn’t love dossiers themselves, of course; they’re for nerds – unless, that is, they’re a “secret dossier”, which have a thrilling redolence of spy dramas, invisible ink and dead drops. Non-secret dossiers, though, are inherently risible: call something a “dossier” in English football and you’re immediately signalling: this is absurd poindextering. Dossiers were preposterous when Don Revie was – imagine the pretension! – drawing up scouting reports on opposing players, and they are preposterous today as Mikel Arteta collates images of rival managers stepping outside their technical area.

Arteta, it should be said, did not use the word “dossier”; rather it was swiftly applied to what he had called “a massive storage of images”. During Arsenal’s 2-0 win against Everton last Saturday, he received his second booking of the season for leaving his technical area. This, it turns out, is another part of the vast conspiracy against Arsenal. Yes, Arteta accepted, he left his technical area (44 times before being booked, according to the former referee Graham Scott), but other managers do it too. “There are managers who have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes [they] leave the touchline – no yellows,” he said. “I am clipping all of that … so if somebody comes to me I can say: ‘I am not in the record yet.’ Somebody else has the record so let’s see. Then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers.”

There are two ways of looking at this. Perhaps it’s genuine. Perhaps Arteta really is a ludicrous Pooterish figure, counting the misdemeanours of others, the worst kind of neighbourhood watch curtain-twitcher who happens also to have been cursed with a persecution complex: “I got a fine because my parking permit was partially obscured, but Mr Emery at No 17 has been six inches out of his bay on at least three occasions this month and … nothing.” Or perhaps he really is an inveterate snitch, glorying in telling on his peers: “Please, Miss! Miss, Daniel’s been chewing gum again, Miss.”

Or, perhaps awed by the misguided defiance of Manchester City fans after their club was found to have perpetrated the greatest act of cheating in English sporting history, he is trying to persuade his base that everybody is against Arsenal to generate a siege mentality. Declan Rice mystifyingly got away with kicking Malick Yalcouyé off the ball against Brighton, but it’s important to remember that Arsenal remain the real victims here.

The history of mind games in football is long and storied. Before the 1939 FA Cup final, for instance, Major Frank Buckley, the flamboyant manager of Wolves, claimed to have injected his players with “animal secretions”. A French surgeon, Serge Voronoff, had begun transplanting tissue from monkey testicles on to human testicles as an anti-ageing treatment, and it was widely believed that it was this monkey gland treatment that Buckley was employing. In fact, he almost certainly gave his players nothing stronger than vitamins but the idea was that Wolves’ morale would be boosted, while their opponents in the final, Portsmouth, would be intimidated by the prospect of taking on players juiced up on simian fluids. It didn’t work, Portsmouth winning 4-1 despite finishing 15 places below Wolves in the table, but the logic is familiar.

The monkey glands were relatively benign, little more than a publicity stunt, but it’s easy for attempts at psychological manipulation to take on a darker aspect. Before Inter played Liverpool in the second leg of the 1965 European Cup semi-final, for instance, their manager, Helenio Herrera, had 100,000 leaflets distributed claiming that at the end of the first leg at Anfield, Liverpool fans had sung “Go home, Italians” to the tune of “Santa Lucia” which supposedly was intended “to deride us and make us feel we are just a race of cheap mandolin players”. Suitably enraged, Inter fans ensured San Siro seethed with fury, which perhaps encouraged some questionable refereeing decisions (although it probably wasn’t the only factor) as Liverpool lost 3-0 and went out 4-3 on aggregate.

Alex Ferguson was a master of the art, while José Mourinho openly acknowledged that the next game begins in the post-match press conference for the previous one. Mourinho, in particular, often crossed the line of professional decency. Arteta, clearly, is not at that level, at least not yet, but if his dossier is part of a deliberate strategy it is a dangerous one.

Arteta’s conspiracy theory is likely to find fertile ground among certain online Arsenal fans, who remain convinced that referees have been machinating against them for years. Even on Tuesday there were those who leaped to the defence of Max Dowman after he had been sent off for thrusting a knee towards Harrison Neal’s chest, even though Arteta himself appeared furious with the 16-year-old’s petulance. Why, ran the argument, had Cole Palmer not been shown a straight red for retaliating against Mateus Fernandes in Chelsea’s defeat by Tottenham on Saturday? Dowman went with his knee and Palmer with his belly, which is perhaps enough to explain the discrepancy, but even if it isn’t, so what? If you don’t want to be punished, don’t go thrusting knees or bellies or anything at opponents, no matter how bad a foul they’ve just committed.

It’s not only that football is groaning under the weight of the paranoia of various fan groups, each adamant that Pro Ref is acting with the rosicrucians, the Masons, the mob, Opus Dei and the Cubans to deny their club a spot in the Europa League, a distraction that deflects from the game’s true crisis: its descent from an endeavour in which sporting merit and integrity are paramount into a grimly capitalistic vehicle to make very rich and powerful people even richer and more powerful.

It’s also dangerous because a mood of insecurity, of being convinced everything is against you, is not conducive to winning league titles – as Arsenal know. In 2024-25, their title bid was undermined by their early-season ill discipline, each red card greeted not with the resilience of champions but with bleating about how it wasn’t really their fault and everybody was picking on them, including the injury gods.
Abdicating responsibility rarely helps, snitches seldom prosper and, in English football, dossiers are always a bad idea.
items.author: Jonathan Wilson
items.titleZh: 若米克尔·阿尔特塔的资料集是一项刻意策略，这对阿森纳来说极其危险 | 乔纳森·威尔逊
items.summaryZh: 阿尔特塔收集对手教练越界的画面引发争议，若此阴谋论是刻意策略，对阿森纳而言将十分危险。
bodyZh: 英格兰足球界喜欢用“资料集（dossier）”这个词。当然，人们并不真正喜欢资料集本身，那是书呆子的玩意——除非它是“秘密资料集”，带有一种间谍剧、隐形墨水和死信箱的刺激氛围。然而，非秘密资料集的本质是可笑的：在英格兰足球中，把某样东西称为“资料集”就是在明确释放信号：这是荒谬的学究气。当唐·里维（Don Revie）——想象一下那种假惺惺的做作——为对手球员制作球探报告时，资料集就显得荒谬，而今天米克尔·阿尔特塔（Mikel Arteta）收集对手教练跨出技术区域的影像时，同样荒谬。

需要指出的是，阿尔特塔本人并没有使用“资料集”这个词；这个词很快就被贴在了他所说的“海量影像存储”上。在上周六阿森纳2-0战胜埃弗顿的比赛中，他因离开技术区域而收到了本赛季的第二张黄牌。事实证明，这是针对阿森纳庞大阴谋的又一部分。是的，阿尔特塔承认他离开了技术区域（据前裁判格雷厄姆·斯科特统计，在被黄牌警告前有44次），但其他教练也这么做。“有些教练在联赛中保持着记录，10分钟内36次离开教练指挥区——却没有黄牌，”他说。“我把所有这些都剪辑下来……所以如果有人来找我说事，我可以回答：‘我的纪录还没到呢。’别人保持着纪录，让我们拭目以待。那么接下来就是10分钟内给教练出示36张黄牌。”

看待这件事有两种方式。也许这是真情流露。也许阿尔特塔真的成了一个荒唐可笑的普特（Pooterish）式人物，数着别人的轻罪，就像那种最糟糕的社区守望相助中爱窥视窗帘的小人，偏巧又患有被害妄想症：“我因为停车证部分被遮挡而罚款，但17号的埃米利县先生这个月至少有三次把车停在车位外面六英寸……却什么事都没有。”或者他真的成了一个根深蒂固的小报告分子，以告发同行为乐：“老师！老师，丹尼又在嚼口香糖了，老师。”
或者，也许是被曼城球迷在俱乐部被发现实施了英格兰体育史上最大作弊行为后表现出的那种被误导的挑衅所震撼，他正试图向其基本盘灌输所有人都在与阿森纳作对的想法，从而营造一种围城心态。德克兰·赖斯（Declan Rice）在对阵布莱顿的比赛中无球踢倒马利克·亚尔库耶（Malick Yalcouyé）却离奇地逃脱了惩罚，但重要的是要记住，阿森纳仍然是这里真正的受害者。

足球界心理战的历史悠久且充满传奇。例如，在1939年足总杯决赛之前，狼队张扬的主帅弗兰克·巴克利（Frank Buckley）少校声称给他的球员注射了“动物分泌物”。一位法国外科医生谢尔盖·沃罗诺夫（Serge Voronoff）曾开始将猴子睾丸组织移植到人类睾丸上作为抗衰老疗法，人们普遍认为巴克利采用的就是这种猴腺疗法。事实上，他给球员使用的东西几乎不可能比维生素更强烈，但其目的是为了提升狼队的士气，同时让决赛对手朴茨茅斯因为要对付注入了类人猿体液的球员而感到畏惧。这并没有起作用，朴茨茅斯以4-1获胜，尽管他们在积分榜上比狼队低了15位，但这种逻辑却是大家熟悉的。

猴腺疗法相对温和，不过是个宣传噱头，但心理战的尝试很容易呈现出更黑暗的一面。例如，在国际米兰对阵利物浦的1965年欧洲冠军杯半决赛次回合之前，他们的主帅海伦尼奥·埃雷拉（Helenio Herrera）散发了10万份传单，声称在安菲尔德的首回合比赛结束后，利物浦球迷曾伴着《圣露西亚》的曲调高唱“回你们的意大利去吧”，这据称旨在“嘲笑我们，让我们觉得我们只是一个廉价曼陀林演奏者的民族”。在被彻底激怒后，国际米兰球迷确保了圣西罗球场怒火中烧，这或许促使裁判做出了一些值得商榷的判决（尽管这可能不是唯一的因素），最终利物浦0-3失利，总比分3-4被淘汰。
亚历克斯·弗格森（Alex Ferguson）是这门艺术的大师，而何塞·穆里尼奥（José Mourinho）则公开承认，下一场比赛是从上一场的赛后新闻发布会开始的。尤其是穆里尼奥，经常越过职业体面的底线。显然，阿尔特塔还没有达到那个水平，至少目前还没有，但如果他的资料集是一项刻意策略，那将是一个危险的策略。

阿尔特塔的阴谋论很可能会在某些在线阿森纳球迷中找到肥沃的土壤，他们仍然坚信裁判多年来一直在密谋对付他们。甚至在周二，还有人跳出来为麦克斯·唐曼（Max Dowman）辩护，此前他因用膝盖撞击哈里森·尼尔（Harrison Neal）的胸部而被罚下，尽管阿尔特塔本人似乎对这位16岁球员的暴躁脾气怒不可遏。反驳的论点是，为什么在切尔西周六输给托特纳姆热刺的比赛中，科尔·帕尔默（Cole Palmer）因对马特乌斯·费尔南德斯（Mateus Fernandes）进行报复而没有被直接红牌罚下？唐曼用的是膝盖，帕尔默用的是肚子，这或许足以解释两者的差异，但即使解释不了，那又怎样？如果你不想受到惩罚，就不要把膝盖、肚子或任何东西撞向对手，无论他们刚才犯规有多严重。

不仅是足球在各种球迷群体的偏执重压下呻吟，每个球迷群体都坚信职业裁判在与玫瑰十字会、共济会、黑帮、主业会和古巴人勾结，剥夺他们俱乐部参加欧联杯的资格，这种干扰转移了人们对足球真正危机的视线：它从一项将体育精神和正直放在首位的运动，沦为了一个严酷的资本主义工具，旨在让非常富有和强大的人变得更加富有和强大。
这也之所以危险，是因为一种不安全感、确信一切都对你不利的氛围，并不利于赢得联赛冠军——正如阿森纳所知。在2024-25赛季，他们的争冠努力由于赛季初期的纪律涣散而受到破坏，每一次红牌迎来的不是冠军的韧性，而是关于错不在他们、所有人都在找他们麻烦（包括伤病之神）的抱怨。
推卸责任很少有帮助，打小报告的人很少能飞黄腾达，而在英格兰足球中，资料集永远都是个坏主意。

bodyEn: Mikel Arteta used a Spanish word to describe what it felt like to be helpless at Anfield while playing for Everton in 2011: bajar. “It’s when a cyclist is going up and looks amazing, then in one kilometre he goes ‘boom’ and he’s struggling again,” he said in Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary. “The game was going well and then suddenly I could only see red shirts flying around. The game is passing all over me and I cannot react. I only had that feeling in my career once, and it was at Anfield.”

Given Arteta’s record at Liverpool, Sunday’s showdown with his childhood friend Andoni Iraola – five days after Arsenal were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Fleetwood – could be expected to fill him with dread. Arteta finally tasted victory there as a player with Arsenal in September 2012, after five failed attempts in the Merseyside derby, but ended up spending the night in hospital with concussion after colliding with Jordan Henderson in an incident he has described as “the biggest fear of my life”.

Arteta was part of the Arsenal side that won at Anfield again six months later thanks to goals from the new signings Lukas Podolski and Santi Cazorla. That was the last time the club triumphed there in the Premier League. They have not won at Anfield for 13 league matches, equalling the club’s worst run at Liverpool. Arsenal’s one victory at Liverpool in the interim came in the League Cup on penalties in 2020 on Arteta’s second visit as a manager.

The Spaniard tried to prepare his players for a trip to Anfield in November 2021 by playing You’ll Never Walk Alone over the training ground speakers but that ended in a 4-0 defeat. He was criticised after last season’s loss in late August, when Dominik Szoboszlai’s late free-kick ended a sequence of three Arsenal draws at Liverpool, for a perceived failure to take off the handbrake, having started Mikel Merino as his No 10. Gary Neville went as far as to say Arsenal lacked “the mentality to go and win big matches at big away grounds”, an assertion that will have hurt Arteta but does have credence: they have not beaten Manchester City in the Premier League at the Etihad since 2015 under Arsène Wenger.

Arteta will be keen to disprove such perceptions, especially after Arsenal struggled so badly against a team 84 places below them in the pyramid in a stadium that holds fewer than 6,000 people. The strikers Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres surprisingly started in tandem at Fleetwood, presumably in an attempt to lighten the load on Martin Ødegaard, although both look badly out of form. Bukayo Saka is out with a thigh injury, there are concerns over Noni Madueke’s ankle and Arsenal’s failed appeal over Max Dowman’s red card rules out the teenager for three matches.

With that in mind, Arteta’s best chance of beating Liverpool is probably by taking the cautious approach that has served him so well and was the cornerstone of last season’s Premier League title triumph. He can take inspiration from one of the most famous nights in Arsenal’s history 37 years ago when George Graham’s side arrived at Anfield needing a 2-0 victory to be champions.

“I told my players to keep things tight in the first half – it was imperative we did not concede,” said Graham in an interview to mark the 20th anniversary of that dramatic finale to the 1988-89 season, when Michael Thomas scored in stoppage time to end Arsenal’s 18-year wait for the title. “The papers were saying we’d have to attack from the off, but I was adamant that was wrong. If Liverpool had scored an early goal it would have been over. But they did very little attacking and played into our hands.”

Before the 1989 game, Arsenal’s players ran to all four corners of the ground to hand flowers to Liverpool fans as a show of sympathy after the Hillsborough disaster the previous month – an idea proposed by their longstanding director Ken Friar, who died this month.

Graham and Arteta were 44 when they won their first league titles and the similarities do not end there. The former Scotland midfielder, who scored almost 80 goals for Arsenal and helped them win the Double in 1971, was known for his emphasis on defending as a manager and “1-0 to the Arsenal” became synonymous with Graham, especially towards the end of his reign. Arteta has revived that tradition since he took over in December 2019, recording 1-0 victories 32 times in the Premier League, more than any club apart from Everton.

Arsenal scored their first set-piece goal of the season in a routine 2-0 win at home to Everton last Saturday and targeting Liverpool’s weakness from set plays while keeping things tight at the other end could be the most effective tactic against a team who have been finding their feet under Iraola in recent weeks.

“Collectively, we acknowledge the importance of defending,” said Arteta last year when asked about comparisons between his team and Graham’s. “We know that if we excel in that part of the game, the chances and the probabilities to win more matches is going to be very, very high.”
Arsenal flew back to London after losing to Fleetwood on penalties in a shootout that will have revived bad memories of May’s Champions League final defeat by Paris Saint-Germain.

The Carabao Cup has stretched Arteta’s squad in the past two seasons, when they reached first the semi-finals then the final, so that is one potential positive from their elimination – not that the ultra-competitive Spaniard would agree. For him, the only way to respond to the most embarrassing night of his managerial career will be to follow in Graham’s footsteps on Sunday.

items.titleZh: 阿尔特塔可从乔治·格拉汉姆身上汲取灵感，抹去安菲尔德的痛苦回忆
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳已在英超客场对阵利物浦13场不胜，阿尔特塔希望效仿前辈格拉汉姆迎来突破。
bodyZh: 米克尔·阿尔特塔曾用一个西班牙语单词来形容2011年效力埃弗顿期间在安菲尔德感到无助时的感受：bajar。“这就像一个骑自行车的人正在爬坡并且表现惊艳，然后在一公里内他突然‘砰’的一声，又开始挣扎了，”他在亚马逊的纪录片《全或无》中说道，“比赛进行得很顺利，然后突然我只能看到红色的球衣在身边飞奔。比赛从我身边掠过，我无法反应。我的职业生涯中只有一次有过这种感觉，那就是在安菲尔德。”
鉴于阿尔特塔在利物浦的战绩，在阿森纳被弗利特伍德淘汰出联赛杯五天后，周日与他童年好友安东尼·伊劳拉的对决可能会让他感到恐惧。在默西塞德郡德比中经历五次失败后，阿尔特塔终于在2012年9月作为阿森纳球员在那里尝到了胜利的滋味，但由于与乔丹·亨德森相撞，他最终因脑震荡在医院度过了一夜，他将这次事件描述为“我一生中最大的恐惧”。
六个月后，凭借新援卢卡斯·波多尔斯基和圣地亚哥·卡索拉的进球，阿尔特塔随阿森纳再次在安菲尔德取胜。那是俱乐部上一次在英超联赛中在那里取胜。他们已经在安菲尔德连续13场联赛未能取胜，追平了俱乐部在利物浦的最差纪录。在此期间，阿森纳在利物浦取得的一场胜利是在2020年联赛杯的点球大战中，这也是阿尔特塔第二次以主教练身份到访。

这位西班牙人曾试图在2021年11月前往安菲尔德前，在训练场的扬声器里播放《你永远不会独行》来为球员做准备，但那场比赛最终以0比4告败。在去年8月下旬失利后，他受到了批评，当时多米尼克·索博斯莱的远射任意球终结了阿森纳在利物浦的三连平，人们认为他没有松开手刹，因为他让米克尔·梅里诺首发出任10号位。加里·内维尔甚至表示阿森纳缺乏“在重要客场赢得重要比赛的心态”，这一言论可能会伤害到阿尔特塔，但确实有其道理：自2015年温格执教以来，他们在英超联赛中从未在阿提哈德球场击败过曼城。
阿尔特塔将渴望打破这种看法，特别是考虑到阿森纳在一个容量不到6000人、且身处低级别联赛84位之遥的球队面前表现得如此挣扎。前锋凯·哈弗茨和维克托·哲凯赖什令人意外地在弗利特伍德联袂首发，这大概是为了减轻马丁·厄德高的负担，尽管两人看起来状态都很糟糕。布卡约·萨卡因大腿受伤缺阵，人们对农尼·马杜埃克的脚踝感到担忧，而阿森纳对马克斯·唐曼红牌的上诉失败也让这名少将面临三场禁赛。
有鉴于此，阿尔特塔击败利物浦的最佳机会可能是采取他擅长的谨慎态度，这也是他上赛季赢得英超冠军的基石。他可以从37年前阿森纳历史上最著名的夜晚之一中汲取灵感，当时乔治·格拉汉姆的球队抵达安菲尔德时，需要一场2-0的胜利才能夺冠。
“我告诉球员们在上半场要保持紧凑——我们绝不能失球，”格拉汉姆在纪念1988-89赛季戏剧性结局20周年的采访中说道，当时迈克尔·托马斯在补时阶段进球，结束了阿森纳长达18年的冠军荒。“报纸上说我们必须从一开始就进攻，但我坚信那是错的。如果利物浦早早进球，比赛就结束了。但他们几乎没有进攻，正合我们心意。”
在1989年的比赛之前，阿森纳球员跑向球场的四个角落，向利物浦球迷献花，以表达对上个月希尔斯堡惨案的同情——这个想法是由他们长期担任总监的肯·弗里尔提出的，他于本月去世。
格拉汉姆和阿尔特塔在赢得他们的第一个联赛冠军时都是44岁，两者的相似之处远不止于此。这位前苏格兰中场曾为阿森纳打入近80球并在1971年帮助他们赢得双冠王，作为主教练，他以强调防守而闻名，“1-0给阿森纳”成为了格拉汉姆的代名词，尤其是在他执教后期。自2019年12月接手以来，阿尔特塔复兴了这一传统，在英超联赛中32次以1-0取胜，除了埃弗顿之外，没有哪家俱乐部比这更多。

上周六，阿森纳在主场2-0轻取埃弗顿，打入了本赛季的第一个定位球，在另一端保持紧凑的同时，针对利物浦在定位球上的弱点，可能是对阵这支最近几周在伊劳拉带领下逐渐找到状态的球队最有效的战术。
“作为一个集体，我们承认防守的重要性，”阿尔特塔去年被问及他的球队与格拉汉姆的球队之间的比较时说道，“我们知道，如果我们能在比赛的那个部分表现出色，赢得更多比赛的机会和概率将会非常非常高。”
在点球大战中负于弗利特伍德后，阿森纳飞回伦敦，这场失利重新唤起了5月份欧冠决赛输给巴黎圣日耳曼的不愉快回忆。
联赛杯在过去两个赛季中拉长了阿尔特塔的阵容，当时他们先是打入半决赛，然后打入决赛，所以这是他们被淘汰带来的一个潜在积极因素——不过这位极具竞争力的西班牙人可不会这么认为。对他来说，回应他执教生涯中最尴尬夜晚的唯一方法，就是周日追随格拉汉姆的脚步。

bodyEn: Every Liverpool win this season seems to come with an asterisk. Yes, they beat Brentford, but Brentford had a man sent off. Yes they beat Villarreal, but they conceded three. On Sunday, against Brighton the asterisks finally ran out. Liverpool beat the Premier League’s top scorers 2-0, kept a clean sheet against a side that had scored 23 goals in their first seven games, and won a league match at home for the first time since April.

Liverpool have won their last five games – including knocking Chelsea out of the Carabao Cup at Anfield on penalties – and are fourth in the Premier League, but there is still the sense that nobody quite trusts what they are watching. Liverpool remain a work in progress, with questions about their ability to create enough chances and break down stubborn opponents. Arsenal’s visit to Anfield this weekend will give us an indication of how much they have progressed under Andoni Iraola.

Given Liverpool’s spending and squad, this fixture should be seen as a title race six-pointer. Signing three attacking players for more than £100m – Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak – brings with it a certain level of expectation. The league table hardly dismisses their case for a title charge. Liverpool are fourth, a point behind Brighton and six adrift of Manchester City and Arsenal. A win at home on Sunday would put them just three points behind the champions. And they have been impressive in the Champions League, winning all three of their games so far to sit third in the 36-team table.

Since the 3-0 home defeat to Manchester City at the start of October, Liverpool have scored 15 goals in five games. Even that defeat at City comes with context. The game was goalless until Ryan Gravenberch’s red card changed it. It is a strong foundation, though cautious Liverpool fans – who have been watching the performances as closely as the results – will tell you there is still plenty to fix.

The fact we are discussing fixes rather than fundamental flaws is, in itself, a sign of how far Liverpool have come since May. In the last days of Arne Slot’s time in charge, their problems could not be solved by moving one piece on a tactics board. They had lost their identity and intensity. The tidy possession, early goals and sharp counterattacks that underpinned their title win disappeared – and Jürgen Klopp’s high-intensity press was long gone. Slot cycled through a 4-2-3-1, a diamond, a 4-5-1 and a back five without finding a system that worked consistently.

With a lack of identity came a struggle to balance an expensively assembled attack with a functioning defence. They conceded 53 goals in the league last season – their highest total since the 1993–94 season, when they had Bruce Grobbelaar in goal. They lost their resilience, too, conceding eight goals after the 90th minute. And they took just five points from losing positions compared with 19 the previous season. By the end of Slot’s time in charge they looked devoid of confidence and conviction.

Those fundamental flaws no longer exist under Iraola. There is a recognisable identity again: a pressing, transition-hungry side designed to win the ball high and feed Alexander Isak, who has six league goals – second only to Erling Haaland in the race for the Premier League golden boot.

Liverpool have kept clean sheets in half of their league games this season, which suggests the balance has returned too. The team presses from the front, confident to commit numbers forward with a settled back line of Ronald Araújo, Virgil van Dijk, Jérémy Jacquet and Milos Kerkez behind them. Araújo has turned the right-back position from a weakness to a strength, bringing some much-needed defensive prowess. And Barcola’s work rate means Iraola can use the attacking talent at his disposal without leaving the defence too exposed.

The fight has returned as well. Twice in the last fortnight, against Brentford and Villarreal, they have fallen behind and won. In fact, Liverpool have already picked up five points from losing positions in the Premier League – as many as they managed in the whole of last season. They are yet to drop a point from a winning position.

So, why are there doubts? The most obvious issue is their lack of goals. Liverpool have scored just 11 goals in their eight league games; eight teams have scored more – Brighton have scored more than twice as many goals as Liverpool. The underlying numbers are also a worry for Liverpool. They have only created six big chances – the second worst tally in the division after Coventry. To put that in some context, Manchester City have created 28 big chances, while Bournemouth, Everton and Brighton have all created 20.

Part of the explanation lies with the way opponents line up against Liverpool. They face a low block more than most sides in the Premier League and rarely face teams that are willing to play out from the back against them. For a side that is built to break at pace and wants to win the ball high up the pitch, there has been a noticeable lack of room to run into. Only one of their 11 fast breaks this season has produced a goal.

The other issue is that, while Isak is scoring, their attack has not yet clicked in the league. Florian Wirtz perhaps symbolises the problem best. He produces plenty of chances but rarely the decisive pass. He has, however, provided two Premier League assists for Víctor Muñoz goals this season and also one for Barcola in the Champions League.

Arsenal will prove an interesting test on Sunday as Liverpool will not face the problem of breaking down a low block. The champions will probably push high at Anfield and try to play in the Liverpool half. That will leave space behind, exactly what Iraola’s side have been missing.

Six months ago, the question was whether Liverpool could solve their fundamental problems. They are a team again: organised, intense and more resilient than in Slot’s last season. Results have been impressive so far but questions remain, namely whether Iraola can establish his high-pressing, transition-heavy approach against sides that play low blocks and still create chances at the rate of title challengers.

items.titleZh: 利物浦是否在争冠行列？他们对阵阿森纳的比赛将说明很多问题
items.summaryZh: 利物浦近期取得五连胜，本周末对阵阿森纳的比赛将检验其真实争冠实力。
bodyZh: 本赛季利物浦的每场胜利似乎都带有某种前提。是的，他们击败了布伦特福德，但对手被罚下一人。是的，他们击败了比利亚雷亚尔，但也丢了三个球。周日对阵布莱顿的比赛终于打破了这种局面。利物浦以2-0击败了英格兰足球超级联赛（英超）进球最多的球队，对阵一支在前七场比赛中打入23球的队伍保持零封，并自4月以来首次在主场赢得联赛比赛。
利物浦已经取得了各项赛事五连胜——包括在安菲尔德通过点球大战将切尔西淘汰出联赛杯——并且在英超积分榜上排名第四，但人们依然觉得没有人完全信任他们眼前的表现。利物浦仍然是一支处于建设中的球队，关于他们创造足够机会以及打破僵局能力的疑问依然存在。本周末阿森纳造访安菲尔德，将让我们看到他们在安多尼·伊劳拉（Andoni Iraola）带领下取得了多大进步。
考虑到利物浦的引援投入和阵容，这场比赛应被视为一场价值六分的争冠对决。签下三名总价超过1亿英镑的攻击手——弗洛里安·维尔茨、布拉德利·巴尔科拉和亚历山大·伊萨克——带来了某种预期的水平。积分榜很难否定他们争夺冠军的理由。利物浦排名第四，落后布莱顿一分，落后曼城和阿森纳六分。周日如果在主场取胜，他们将仅落后卫冕冠军三分。他们在欧冠赛场上也表现出色，前三场比赛全胜，在36支球队的积分榜上排名第三。
自从10月初主场0-3负于曼城以来，利物浦在五场比赛中打入了15球。即便是那场对阵曼城的失利也有其背景。在瑞安·格拉芬贝赫被红牌罚下之前，比赛一直没有进球。这是一个坚实的基础，不过谨慎的利物浦球迷——他们一直在密切关注比赛表现和比赛结果——会告诉你，仍有很多问题需要解决。

我们讨论的是需要修正的地方，而不是根本性的缺陷，这本身就说明了利物浦自5月以来取得了多大的进步。在阿尔内·斯洛特（Arne Slot）执教的最后日子里，他们的问题无法通过在战术板上移动一个棋子来解决。他们失去了自己的身份和强度。支撑他们赢得冠军的整洁控球、早早进球和犀利反击已经消失了——而尤尔根·克洛普（Jürgen Klopp）的高强度逼抢也早已不复存在。斯洛特尝试过4-2-3-1、菱形中场、4-5-1和五后卫，但始终没有找到一个能持续发挥作用的体系。
随着身份认同的缺失，他们难以将高价组建的进攻线与运转良好的防守平衡起来。上赛季他们在联赛中丢了53球——这是自1993-94赛季拥有布鲁斯·格罗贝尔拉（Bruce Grobbelaar）守门以来的最高失球纪录。他们也失去了韧性，在第90分钟后丢了八球。与前一个赛季从落后局面中拿到19分相比，他们上赛季在落后局面下只得到了5分。在斯洛特执教结束时，他们看起来毫无自信和信念。
在伊劳拉的手下，这些根本性的缺陷已不复存在。他们重新拥有了清晰可辨的足球风格：一支渴望逼抢、注重攻防转换的球队，旨在在前场赢得球权并输送给亚历山大·伊萨克，后者已经打入6个联赛进球，在英超金靴争夺战中仅次于埃尔林·哈兰德。
利物浦本赛季有一半的联赛比赛保持零封，这表明球队的平衡也已经回归。球队从前场开始逼抢，在身后由罗纳德·阿劳霍、弗吉尔·范戴克、热雷米·雅凯和米洛斯·凯尔克兹组成的稳定后防线支持下，充满信心地将兵力投入前场。阿劳霍将右后卫位置从弱点变成了强项，带来了急需的防守能力。巴尔科拉的工作投入意味着伊劳拉可以在不让防线过于暴露的情况下，利用手头的进攻天赋。
斗志也已经回归。在过去的两周里，面对布伦特福德和比利亚雷亚尔，他们曾两度落后并最终逆转取胜。事实上，利物浦在英超联赛中已经在落后局面下拿到了五分——这与他们上赛季全年的总积分相当。他们还没有在领先后丢失过分数。
那么，为什么还会有疑问？最明显的问题是他们缺乏进球。利物浦在八场联赛中仅打入11球；有八支球队的进球数超过他们——布莱顿的进球数甚至是利物浦的两倍多。底层数据也让利物浦感到担忧。他们只创造了6次绝佳机会——在联赛中排名倒数第二，仅次于考文垂。相比之下，曼城创造了28次绝佳机会，而伯恩茅斯、埃弗顿和布莱顿都创造了20次。
部分原因在于对手对阵利物浦时的排兵布阵。与英超绝大多数球队相比，他们更多地面临低位防守，而且很少遇到愿意从后场组织进攻的对手。对于一支习惯于快速反击并希望在高位赢得球权的球队来说，明显的空间不足。他们本赛季的11次快攻中只有一次转化为了进球。
另一个问题是，虽然伊萨克正在进球，但他们的锋线在联赛中尚未完全产生化学反应。弗洛里安·维尔茨或许最能象征这个问题。他创造了大量机会，但很少送出决定性的传球。不过，他在本赛季的英超联赛中为维克托·穆尼奥斯送出了两次助攻，还在欧冠中为巴尔科拉送出了一次助攻。
阿森纳将在周日证明这是一场有趣的测试，因为利物浦不会面临破密集防守的难题。卫冕冠军可能会在安菲尔德压得很高，并试图在利物浦的半场展开比赛。这将留下身后空间，这正是伊劳拉的球队一直在寻找的。
六个月前，问题在于利物浦能否解决他们的根本问题。他们重新成为了一支团队：比斯洛特执教的最后一个赛季更有组织性、强度更高且更具韧性。迄今为止的战果令人印象深刻，但疑问依然存在，即伊劳拉能否在面对采取低位防守的球队时，依然建立起他的高位逼抢、注重转换的打法，并以争冠球队的速度创造机会。
这是一篇由WhoScored发布的文章。

items.titleEn: ‘We are not in Disneyland’: Arteta warns Dowman of Arsenal’s demands
items.summaryEn: ‘We have made these mistakes … you can get punished’Dowman lost appeal against red card at FleetwoodMikel Arteta has warned Max Dowman that he “is not in Disneyland” and must learn from his red card against Fleetwood after Arsenal’s appeal against his three-match suspension was rejected.The 16-year-old became the youngest player ever to be sent off in the League Cup on Tuesday as the Premier League champions crashed out to the League Two side Fleetwood. Arteta said he was “very disappointed” that the Football Association rejected the appeal against his red card and felt Dowman was lucky not to suffer a broken foot from “reckless tackles”. Continue reading...
bodyEn: Mikel Arteta has warned Max Dowman that he “is not in Disneyland” and must learn from his red card against Fleetwood after Arsenal’s appeal against his three-match suspension was rejected.

The 16-year-old became the youngest player ever to be sent off in the League Cup on Tuesday as the Premier League champions crashed out to the League Two side Fleetwood. Arteta said he was “very disappointed” that the Football Association rejected the appeal against his red card and felt Dowman was lucky not to suffer a broken foot from “reckless tackles”.

But despite describing his reaction as “minimal”, the Arsenal manager revealed he had spoken to Dowman this week to underline his responsibilities after he was also sent off this month playing for England Under 19s.

“I’ve done it, so I try to prevent that [in future]. That’s why I’m so protective of these things and especially with young players, because we have made those mistakes. You know how much you can get punished and how much it can change what happens next, and it’s not the first time, so obviously we need to put an end to it very, very quickly,” Arteta said.

Arteta said he had not seen the criticism of his angry reaction to Dowman’s red card, when he appeared to aim a few choice words towards the forward as he headed down the tunnel. But he defended his actions after warning Dowman he was likely to be targeted before the game. “It’s something that we discussed just before we went out, because it’s not the first time that happened,” he said.

“For me, it was the best reaction ever to be able to be who I am. You want to see the reaction of his teammates? When they have to play with 10, you want to see that? That’s the level, and that’s the reaction. But the reaction when I don’t win, you know what the reaction is? I’m pissed off, big time.

“So we need to be ready for that. This is the environment and this is the reality. Otherwise, we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland. We are in the Premier League at this level and we look after him so much that you cannot imagine. But at the same time, we’re going to demand [from] him like anybody else because he needs to earn the right to play.”

Dowman will be suspended for Sunday’s trip to Liverpool and the games against Hull and Newcastle, while Noni Madueke faces a late test to see if he has recovered from an ankle problem that kept him out of the game against Fleetwood. Arteta also revealed that Bukayo Saka is not expected back until at least after the international break as Arsenal await more news on his thigh injury.

Arteta said they had “put every argument on the table” in an attempt to clear Dowman’s name but to no avail. “Very disappointed,” he said. “Especially with the reckless tackles that he received, and then his reaction is minimal in relation to the action.
“I think you have to read the context of the player, the age, and what happened previously. It could have been really bad. And we are lucky today that he hasn’t had a broken foot. That’s clear.”

items.titleZh: 阿尔特塔警告多曼：这里不是迪士尼乐园
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳对多曼红牌上诉被驳回，阿尔特塔警告他需吸取教训并承担责任。
bodyZh: 在阿森纳对多曼三场禁赛的上诉被驳回后，米克尔·阿尔特塔警告马克斯·多曼，他“不是在迪士尼乐园里”，必须从对阵弗利特伍德时的红牌中吸取教训。
这位16岁球员于周二成为联赛杯历史上被罚下的最年轻球员，当时这支英超冠军球队爆冷出局，负于英乙球队弗利特伍德。阿尔特塔表示，他对英足总驳回红牌上诉感到“非常失望”，并认为多曼在遭遇“恶意犯规”时很幸运没有导致断脚。
尽管阿尔特塔形容多曼的反应是“微乎其微的”，但这位阿森纳主帅透露，他本周已经与多曼进行了交流，强调了后者的责任，因为他在本月代表英格兰U19比赛时也被罚下过。
阿尔特塔说：“我已经这么做了，所以我试图（在未来）防止这种情况发生。这就是为什么我如此保护这些事情，尤其是对年轻球员，因为我们犯过那些错误。你知道你会受到多大的惩罚，这会多大程度上改变接下来发生的事情，而且这已经不是第一次了，所以很显然我们需要尽快彻底制止这种情况。”
阿尔特塔表示，他没有看到外界对他在多曼染红时表现出的愤怒情绪的批评，当时他在多曼走向球员通道时似乎对这名前锋说了几句重话。但他为自己的行为进行了辩护，并透露赛前就警告过多曼可能会成为被针对的目标。“这是我们出场前刚刚讨论过的事情，因为这已经不是第一次发生了，”他说。
“对我来说，能够做我自己就是最好的反应。你想看看他的队友们的反应吗？当他们不得不以10人应战时，你想看看那个吗？这就是水平，这就是反应。但当我没有赢球时，你知道我的反应是什么吗？我非常、非常生气。”
“所以我们需要为此做好准备。这就是环境，这就是现实。否则，我们就身处迪士尼乐园了。我们不在迪士尼乐园。我们身处这个水平的英超联赛，我们对他的照顾是你无法想象的。但与此同时，我们将像要求其他人一样要求他，因为他必须通过努力赢得比赛的权利。”
多曼将错过周日客场对阵利物浦的比赛以及对阵赫尔城和纽卡斯尔的比赛，而马杜埃凯则面临最后测试，以确定他是否从缺席对阵弗利特伍德比赛的脚踝伤势中恢复。阿尔特塔还透露，在阿森纳等待萨卡大腿伤势的更多消息期间，预计他至少要到国际比赛日之后才能复出。
阿尔特塔表示，他们已经“提出了所有论据”试图洗清多曼的罪名，但无济于事。“非常失望，”他说。“特别是考虑到他遭到了恶意犯规，而与这一动作相比，他的反应是微乎其微的。”
“我认为你必须结合球员的背景、年龄以及之前发生的事情来理解。情况本可能会非常糟糕。我们今天很幸运，他的脚没有骨折。这是显而易见的。”

items.titleEn: Celebrating Wrighty’s legacy together with adidas
items.summaryEn: Together with adidas, we have officially launched a special and exclusive range
bodyEn: Today, adidas and Arsenal have launched their latest collection, celebrating the career of club legend Ian Wright OBE.

The range, created in collaboration and with creative input from Ian, includes some of his best moments and memories from his Arsenal past, designed with unique hand-drawn illustrations.Combining the best in adidas pre-match and travelwear, the black and white range includes a short and long-sleeved pre-match jersey in men’s, women’s and youth sizes, a reversible anthem jacket, and a cross-body shoulder bag. The design features a patchwork, hand-drawn illustration effect with a variety of squares inspired by Ian’s vibrant personality, the history of his life, people who are close to him and a selection of his favourite memories from his career.

The supporting campaign takes an off-beat look at Ian’s mind, with animated “Wisdoms from Wrighty”, and supporting imagery featuring fellow icons Kelly Smith and David Seaman, as well as current players David Raya, Gabriel Jesus, Katie McCabe, Eddie Nketiah, Kim Little and Gabriel who have all been styled by the man himself.

Wright said: “Turning 60 last month made me reflect a lot on what I’ve done so far, my time at Arsenal and the very special people I’ve worked with. So, to work with adidas and Arsenal on this range that represents some of my biggest career moments is really special. I hope people feel the love in this collection as much as I do.”Inigo Turner, head of design at adidas, said: “Ian has had a hugely successful career with Arsenal, with many memories and moments, and so to mark his 60th birthday, we were keen to capture some of those occasions through innovative hand-drawn illustrations. "We looked back at many of the moments on and off the pitch, and have created a jersey, jacket and bag which we believe really embodies Ian’s style. The black and white patchwork effect takes inspiration from some of his style choices from the 90s, and the pops of gold represent the Golden Boot award he received in 1992, and his iconic gold tooth.“The range was made in total collaboration with Ian, who had a real input into the design process, and it was a pleasure working with him.”

The collection will be worn by both the men’s and women’s team from Saturday, December 2 when our men’s team will warm up in the jersey and walk out in the jacket ahead of their home Premier League game against Wolverhampton Wanderers. Arsenal Women will first wear the range in their upcoming WSL match against Chelsea, also at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday, December 10. Both teams will continue to wear the range for the remainder of the season.The collection is available at Arsenal official club stores and from today.

items.titleZh: 阿森纳携手阿迪达斯共同致敬伊恩·赖特的传奇生涯
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳联手阿迪达斯推出致敬传奇伊恩·赖特的专属系列装备。
bodyZh: 今天，阿迪达斯与阿森纳联合推出了最新系列产品，旨在致敬俱乐部传奇人物伊恩·赖特（Ian Wright OBE）的辉煌职业生涯。
该系列由伊恩参与合作并融入了创意，涵盖了他在阿森纳效力期间的一些最佳时刻和美好回忆，并采用独特的手绘插图进行设计。这一黑白系列结合了阿迪达斯最优秀的赛前热身装备和旅行服饰，包括男女及青少年尺码的长袖和短袖赛前热身球衣、一件可双面穿着的入场夹克以及一个斜挎单肩包。设计采用了拼贴手绘插图效果，并带有各种方块图案，灵感源自伊恩充满活力的个性、他的人生经历、与他亲近的人以及他职业生涯中精选的难忘时刻。
相关的宣传活动以别开生面的方式展现了伊恩的内心世界，其中包含动画形式的“赖特智慧之语”，支持影像还邀请了俱乐部名宿凯利·史密斯（Kelly Smith）和大卫·希曼（David Seaman），以及现役球员大卫·拉亚、加布里埃尔·热苏斯、凯蒂·麦凯布、埃迪·恩凯蒂亚、金·利特尔和加布里埃尔，他们都由伊恩本人亲自进行了造型设计。

赖特表示：“上个月我度过了60岁生日，这让我对过去所做的事情、在阿森纳的时光以及共事过的特别的人进行了很多反思。因此，能与阿迪达斯和阿森纳合作推出这个代表我职业生涯一些最重要时刻的系列，真的非常特别。我希望人们能像我一样，感受到这个系列中所包含的爱意。”阿迪达斯设计总监伊尼戈·特纳（Inigo Turner）表示：“伊恩在阿森纳度过了非常成功的职业生涯，拥有许多美好的记忆和时刻，因此为了庆祝他的60岁生日，我们渴望通过创新的手绘插图捕捉其中一些难忘的场合。我们回顾了他在球场内外的许多瞬间，并设计了一款球衣、夹克和背包，我们相信它们真正体现了伊恩的风格。黑白拼贴效果的灵感来自于他在90年代的一些风格选择，而点缀其间的金色则代表了他在1992年获得的金靴奖以及他标志性的金牙。这个系列是在与伊恩的完全合作下完成的，他在设计过程中提出了真正的创意，与他合作非常愉快。”
男女一线队将于12月2日星期六开始穿着该系列产品。当天，我们的男子队将在主场对阵狼队的英超比赛赛前热身时穿着该球衣，并身穿该夹克步入球场。阿森纳女子队将于12月10日星期日同样在酋长球场进行的对阵切尔西的女子英超联赛中首次穿戴这一系列。两支球队将在本赛季剩余时间内继续穿着该系列产品。该系列产品从今天起在阿森纳官方俱乐部商店发售。

items.titleEn: Arsenal reach 100 consecutive top-flight seasons
items.summaryEn: The 2025/26 campaign will see us complete a century at the top of the English game, having played in the top tier since 1919
bodyEn: The 2025/26 Premier League season be a historic one for the club as we enter our 100th consecutive top-flight season.
Since we were elected to the old First Division in 1919/20, we have been a fixture in the top tier for a century of campaigns, a feat that no other club in English football history comes close to.
Over our first 99 seasons, we contested 4,024 games; game number 4,025 saw us beat Manchester United 1-0 at Old Trafford to secure win number 1,900 in that time.

It was back in 1904/05 when the club - then known as Woolwich Arsenal - first sampled life in England’s top-flight, spending seven seasons at that level before suffering the only relegation in our history back in 1913 - the same year we moved to Highbury.

After two seasons in Division Two, football was suspended due to the outbreak of World War I. When play resumed in 1919, the Football League was expanded, and we benefited by being selected to join the First Division, where we have remained ever since.
We have held the record for the longest top-flight tenure since 1983/84, which was our 58th consecutive season at that level, surpassing Sunderland’s 57-season stint from 1891 to 1958.

Five of the six longest top-flight spells are ongoing, which sees all the Premier League ever-presents included except Chelsea, who will play a 37th-straight season in the top-flight this term. Aside from those six, Manchester City are the side with the next longest run - 24 since they were promoted in 2003/04.
Showing how staggering our achievement is, Leicester City have suffered 12 relegations to the second tier during our 100-season stint, while six other teams have endured that fate on nine occasions.
We boast a win percentage of 47% across our 100 seasons, winning the championship on 13 occasions, including at least one in seven different decades.

As for those who have contributed most during that time, no player has appeared in more of our 4,024 games than David O'Leary, who is approaching the 50th anniversary of his debut back in 1975, with four-time title-winning captain Tony Adams in second spot.

And it is no surprise to see Thierry Henry on top of the tree when it comes to most goals netted, with 175 of our talisman's record haul of 228 coming in the Premier League. Meanwhile, no manager took charge of more matches than Arsene Wenger's tally of 828 between 1996 and 2018.

Putting our three-figure achievement in further perspective, when looking further afield only Inter Milan are on a longer top-flight tenure in one of Europe’s top five major leagues, a run of 116 years. Notably, Celtic hold the world record for 129 straight seasons in Scotland’s highest tier, while Northern Ireland trio Cliftonville, Glentoran and Linfield have played in 125 straight top-tier seasons.

Uruguayan side Penarol have reached 122 campaigns, while Flamengo have hit 113 in Brazil, with Boca Juniors one behind in Argentina. Ajax have spent 107 seasons at the top level of Dutch football, while Barcelona, Real Madrid and Athletic Club are the only clubs never to be relegated from La Liga since its inception 96 years ago.

items.titleZh: 阿森纳达成顶级联赛连续100个赛季里程碑
items.summaryZh: 2025/26赛季将见证阿森纳在英格兰顶级联赛的第100个赛季。
bodyZh: 2025/26赛季对阿森纳而言将是一个具有历史意义的赛季，我们将迎来在顶级联赛中的第100个连续赛季。
自从我们在1919/20赛季入选老英甲联赛以来，我们在顶级联赛中已经历了一个世纪的征程，这一壮举是英格兰足球历史上其他任何俱乐部都无法企及的。
在我们前99个赛季中，我们共踢了4024场比赛；第4025场比赛是在老特拉福德球场以1比0击败曼联，取得了那段时期的第1900场胜利。
早在1904/05赛季，当时名为伍尔维奇阿森纳的俱乐部首次体验了英格兰顶级联赛的生活，在那个级别踢了七个赛季后，于1913年遭遇了队史唯一一次降级——这也是我们搬迁到海布里的同年。
在乙级联赛踢了两个赛季后，由于第一次世界大战爆发，足球比赛暂停。1919年比赛恢复时，足球联盟进行了扩军，我们很幸运地被选中加入甲联赛并一直留到现在。
自1983/84赛季以来，我们一直保持着顶级联赛最长连续参赛时间的纪录，当时那是我们在这个级别的第58个连续赛季，超越了桑德兰从1891年到1958年保持的57个赛季纪录。
在六个最长的顶级联赛参赛纪录中，有五个仍在延续，其中包括除了切尔西之外所有的英超元老球队，切尔西本赛季将迎来他们的顶级联赛第37个连续赛季。除了这六支球队之外，曼城是参赛时间第二长的球队，自从2003/04赛季升级以来已有24个赛季。
为了展现我们这一成就的惊人之处，在我们的100个赛季期间，莱斯特城曾12次降入第二级别联赛，而其他六支球队也曾九次遭遇这种命运。
在我们100个赛季的历程中，我们的胜率达到了47%，赢得了13次顶级联赛冠军，且在七个不同的十年中都至少夺冠一次。
至于在那段时期贡献最大的人，大卫·奥利里的出场次数超过了我们的4024场比赛中的任何其他球员，他即将迎来20世纪70年代（1975年）上演首秀的50周年纪念，四次夺得冠军的队长托尼·亚当斯位居第二。
毫无疑问，当谈到进球最多时，蒂埃里·亨利高居榜首，这位核心球员创纪录的228粒进球中有175粒是在英超联赛中打进的。与此同时，在1996年至2018年期间，没有任何一位主教练的带队场次能超过阿尔塞纳·温格的828场。
为了进一步展现我们三位数的伟大成就，放眼欧洲五大联赛，只有国际米兰在顶级联赛中的连续参赛时间更长，达到了116年。值得一提的是，凯尔特人保持着苏格兰顶级联赛连续129个赛季的世界纪录，而北爱尔兰的三支球队克利夫顿维尔、格伦托兰和林field则连续参加了125个顶级联赛赛季。
乌拉圭的佩纳罗尔俱乐部达到了122个赛季，巴西的弗拉门戈达到了113个赛季，阿根廷的博卡青年落后一个赛季。阿贾克斯在荷兰顶级联赛度过了107个赛季，而巴塞罗那、皇家马德里和毕尔巴鄂竞技是自96年前西甲创立以来从未降级的仅有俱乐部。

items.titleEn: How our Lionesses led England to Euros glory
items.summaryEn: Check out the facts and stats behind our Lionesses after Euro 2025
bodyEn: Five Arsenal players featured prominently for two-time champions England at UEFA Women’s Euro 2025, with each contributing at the top of their game.

Our friends at Opta have selected some standout facts and stats for each of Leah Williamson, Beth Mead, Chloe Kelly, Alessia Russo and Michelle Agyemang, highlighting how important they were to the nations’ success.
Always on the front foot and recognising danger, captain Williamson won possession in the defensive third 24 times, five more than any other player at the tournament.
A special mention also goes to Lia Walti, who came sixth in that leaderboard with 15 wins of possession despite Switzerland being knocked out in the quarter-finals.

Up top, Russo led all England players for goal involvements, with only Alexia Putellas registering more among all players. That’s because, although Russo only netted twice herself, including the all-important equaliser in the final against Spain, she also provided three assists for her teammates.
Again, she’s not the only Gunner in the top table, with Stina Blackstenius contributing to four Sweden goals, while Mariona Caldentey did the same for runners-up Spain.
Kelly’s impact off the bench can’t be underestimated. She created 10 chances at the tournament - the most of any substitute, with Beth Mead also creating four when she was brought on.
Speaking of Mead, she became the first player on record (since 2013) to both score and assist a goal in four different games at a Women’s EURO, with her goal and assist from the bench against Wales.

Meanwhile, Young Player of the Tournament Agyemang became just the third teenager to score more than once at a major tournament for England (men’s and women’s), after Michael Owen (1998 World Cup) and Wayne Rooney (Euro 2004).

items.summaryZh: 数据盘点阿森纳球员在2025欧洲杯上的出色表现。
bodyZh: 在2025年欧足联女足欧洲杯上，五名阿森纳球员在两届冠军英格兰队的阵中大放异彩，每位球员都在各自的巅峰状态下作出了贡献。
我们在Opta的数据合作伙伴为莉亚·威廉姆森、贝丝·米德、克洛伊·凯利、阿莱西亚·鲁索和米歇尔·阿吉曼挑选了一些突出的事实与数据，突显了她们对国家队成功的重要性。
队长威廉姆森始终保持积极进攻并敏锐察觉危险，她在防守三区赢得球权的次数达到24次，比本届赛事中的任何其他球员都多出5次。
特别值得一提的是利亚·瓦尔蒂，尽管瑞士队在四分之一决赛中被淘汰，她在该项榜单上仍以15次赢得球权排名第六。
在前场，鲁索在英格兰队内的参与进球数居首，在所有球员中也仅次于阿莱克西亚·普特利亚斯。尽管鲁索自己只打进两球，包括决赛对阵西班牙时至关重要的扳平比分，但她还为队友送出了三次助攻。
同样，她并不是唯一上榜的阿森纳球员，斯蒂娜·布莱克斯蒂纽斯为瑞典队贡献了四个进球，马里奥娜·卡尔德恩泰也为亚军西班牙队做出了同样的贡献。
凯利替补登场的冲击力不容忽视。她在本届赛事中创造了10次机会，是所有替补球员中最多的，贝丝·米德在替补出场时也创造了4次机会。
说到米德，她在对阵威尔士队的比赛中替补登场并贡献传射，成为女足欧洲杯历史上自2013年有统计以来，首位在四场不同比赛中均能单场完成传射的球员。
与此同时，赛事最佳年轻球员阿吉曼成为了继迈克尔·欧文（1998年世界杯）和韦恩·鲁尼（2004年欧洲杯）之后，第三位在英格兰成年国家队（男女足）大赛中进球超过一次的青少年球员。

items.titleEn: Jurrien Timber stars in the PL's Big Interview
items.summaryEn: Jurrien Timber reveals all on his dream of playing for Arsenal, coming back from injury and more
bodyEn: Playing for Arsenal is an ambition shared by thousands of young footballers around the world, a dream Jurrien Timber realised when he joined us in 2023.
Our Dutch defender missed out on the majority of last season through injury, but has come back with a bang this season, making 47 appearances to take his Arsenal total to 50.
Speaking recently in the Big Interview with the Premier League at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, Timber recalled the special feeling of signing for his boyhood club.

“It’s always been a dream to play here, definitely… you can tell they’re really building something here. So the moment they came as well it was like, deep down in my heart, I knew, okay, this is my club, I want to play for them.

“The first conversations, you could tell this is a different level, this is a big club, obviously that summer as well, I think they bought Declan, Kai and David. They were making some big moves and I just wanted to be a part of that really bad.”

Making the move to Arsenal is a big moment in any player’s career, but our full-back has been dreaming of wearing the famous red and white since he and his family were watching us in his early childhood.

“I think my oldest brother was an Arsenal fan, my mum as well, so you just kind of take over. We always watched Arsenal when we were young at home, and then you just become a fan. The players, I always like the style of just the club. Then you get some kind of love for a club as well, which started really young.

Jurrien has been a first-team regular this season, but was limited to just three appearances last season after picking up an ACL injury on his Premier League debut. But, positive as ever, our number 12 saw his recovery period as a learning opportunity, and spoke about the experience of watching from the sidelines.

“I could feel after that period that I have some good people around me, and I think that’s really important. Without them, I couldn’t come back like I’ve done this season. Also, the people around me at the club, but also at home, just talking about faith, believing, holding on to that, that helps.
“You’re looking at the team and you’re like, wow, they’re that good! The level is really high, if I want to join this team, I have to be on the same level.”
When Timber did get back on the pitch, he continued a long-standing tradition of Dutch players representing Arsenal at the highest level, something the defender is very proud of.

“I think it’s a beautiful thing to see, hopefully, I can do that as well! [Dennis] Bergkamp was here at a game, it was a couple of months ago I spoke with him. [Marc} Overmars I know from my time at Ajax, [Robin] van Persie is the head coach at Feyenoord with [his brother] Quinten, I don’t speak to them but I know them well.
Timber went on to discuss how much he enjoys playing in a defence as formidable as ours, especially with the emergence of Myles Lewis-Skelly this season.

“It’s incredible. I want to say the kid, but he’s not a kid anymore. I think he’s so mature, he’s special. He does it on the biggest stage, which I know from playing is not easy. He just does it and outside the pitch he’s so nice and kind, you don’t see the lion that comes out inside the pitch, which I really love to see.
“But the whole backline, I think the level is insane. I think we push each other and I’m just lucky to be a part of it.”
Watch the full interview at the top of the article to find out more about Timber’s experiences with the Dutch national team, his hopes for the rest of the season and his time at Ajax.
